source.text: וַיִּרְגַּ֣ז הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיַּ֛עַל עַל־עֲלִיַּ֥ת הַשַּׁ֖עַר וַיֵּ֑בְךְּ וְכֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר בְּלֶכְתּ֗וֹ בְּנִ֤י אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ בְּנִ֣י בְנִ֣י אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מִֽי־יִתֵּ֤ן מוּתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י תַחְתֶּ֔יךָ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּנִ֥י בְנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And was shaken the king, and went up to [the] upper room of the gate and wept; and thus he said as he went, my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Who will give my dying, I, instead of you, Absalom my son, my son!

en.L: And the king was shaken, and he went up to the upper room of the gate and wept. And thus he said as he went: "My son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Who would grant [that] I had died, I myself, instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son!"
en.B: The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gate and wept, and as he went, these were his words: "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I could have died in your place, Absalom, my son, my son!"
en.R: The king was deeply shaken. He went up to the room above the city gate and cried. As he went up, this is what he said: "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I could have died in your place! Absalom, my son, my son!"

es.L: Y el rey se estremeció, y subió a la sala de arriba de la puerta y lloró. Y mientras iba, decía así: «¡Mi hijo Absalón, mi hijo, mi hijo Absalón! ¡Quién concediera que yo hubiera muerto, yo mismo, en tu lugar, Absalón, mi hijo, mi hijo!».
es.B: El rey quedó deshecho. Subió al cuarto que había encima de la puerta y lloró, y mientras subía, estas eran sus palabras: «¡Absalón, hijo mío! ¡Hijo mío, Absalón, hijo mío! ¡Si yo hubiera podido morir en tu lugar, Absalón, hijo mío, hijo mío!».
es.R: El rey quedó profundamente conmovido. Subió al cuarto que estaba encima de la puerta de la ciudad, y lloró. Mientras subía, decía: «¡Absalón, hijo mío! ¡Hijo mío, Absalón, hijo mío! ¡Cómo quisiera haber muerto yo en vez de ti! ¡Absalón, hijo mío, hijo mío!».

fr.L: Et le roi fut bouleversé, et il monta à la chambre haute de la porte et pleura. Et il disait ainsi en marchant : « Mon fils Absalom, mon fils, mon fils Absalom ! Qui me donnerait d’être mort, moi, à ta place, Absalom, mon fils, mon fils ! »
fr.B: Le roi fut bouleversé. Il monta dans la chambre au-dessus de la porte et pleura, et tout en montant il disait : « Mon fils Absalom ! Mon fils, mon fils Absalom ! Si seulement j’avais pu mourir à ta place, Absalom, mon fils, mon fils ! »
fr.R: Le roi a été profondément bouleversé. Il est monté dans la pièce au-dessus de la porte de la ville et il a pleuré. En montant, il disait : « Mon fils Absalom ! Mon fils, mon fils Absalom ! Si seulement j’étais mort à ta place ! Absalom, mon fils, mon fils ! »

vi.L: Vua rúng động, đi lên phòng trên cổng thành mà khóc. Vừa đi vua vừa nói thế này: "Áp-sa-lôm con ơi, con của cha, con của cha, Áp-sa-lôm! Ai cho cha được chết, chính cha, thay cho con, Áp-sa-lôm, con ơi, con ơi!"
vi.B: Vua chấn động. Vua đi lên căn phòng phía trên cổng thành mà khóc, vừa đi vừa than: "Áp-sa-lôm con ơi! Con ơi, Áp-sa-lôm con ơi! Phải chi cha được chết thay cho con, Áp-sa-lôm, con ơi, con ơi!"
vi.R: Vua vô cùng đau đớn. Vua đi lên căn phòng phía trên cổng thành và khóc. Vừa đi lên, vua vừa than: "Áp-sa-lôm con ơi! Con ơi, Áp-sa-lôm con ơi! Phải chi cha được chết thay cho con! Áp-sa-lôm, con ơi, con ơi!"

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in the Hebrew text chapter 19 begins here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. Many Bibles print this verse as the last verse of chapter 18 (18:33), and so number the rest of this chapter one lower: verses 2-44 here are 19:1-43 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: was shaken: trembled with grief and shock
decisions.reason: The verb describes a body or a heart shaken by strong feeling, whether fear, anger or grief (Exodus 15:14; Habakkuk 3:16). Here the news of Absalom's death, just given by the Cushite (18:32), shakes the king to the core.

decisions.choice: the upper room of the gate: a room built over the gateway of Mahanaim
decisions.reason: David had been waiting "between the two gates" for news of the battle (18:24). City gates were thick structures with a room above the passage, and the king climbs to it to grieve out of sight of the people.

decisions.choice: who would grant my dying: a wish, "if only I had died"
decisions.reason: "Who will give ...?" is a fixed Hebrew way of saying "if only" (Exodus 16:3; Deuteronomy 28:67). The added "I" stresses David himself: he wishes he had died instead of his son.

decisions.choice: my son ... my son ...: a broken cry, repeated
decisions.reason: "My son" comes five times and Absalom's name three times in one short cry. The repetition is the grief itself, and every level keeps it rather than smoothing it into one sentence.

decisions.choice: If only I could have died in your place
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the Hebrew "Who would grant ...?" into the plain English wish "If only". "In your place" keeps the sense of the preposition, which means "instead of" or "in the place of".

decisions.choice: "Qui me donnerait d’être mort, moi, à ta place"
alternatives: "Si seulement j’étais mort à ta place"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew form of the wish, a question with "who will give" (m4), which French can still say in a high register; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary "si seulement".

decisions.choice: ¡Quién concediera que yo hubiera muerto ...! (L); ¡Si yo hubiera podido morir en tu lugar ...! (B); ¡Cómo quisiera haber muerto yo en vez de ti! (R)
alternatives: ¡Ojalá hubiera muerto yo en tu lugar!
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew wish 'who will give', with 'quién concediera'; Balanced and Readable give the wish in words of their own, as the terms note asks for this well-known lament, so as not to follow a familiar Spanish version.

decisions.choice: David calls himself "cha" in his lament
decisions.reason: He cries out to his dead son as a father, so the father-and-son forms are used, not the king's "ta"; the repeated "con ơi" carries the broken cry (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "Ai cho cha được chết" (L); "Phải chi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "Who would grant ...?" form of a wish; Balanced and Readable use the plain Vietnamese "if only".

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לְיוֹאָ֑ב הִנֵּ֨ה הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ בֹּכֶ֛ה וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֖ל עַל־אַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to Joab, look, the king [is] weeping, and he mourned for Absalom.

en.L: And it was told to Joab, "Look, the king [is] weeping, and he is mourning for Absalom."
en.B: Joab was told, "The king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."
en.R: Someone told Joab, "The king is crying and mourning for Absalom."

es.L: Y se le informó a Joab: «He aquí, el rey llora, y hace duelo por Absalón».
es.B: Le avisaron a Joab: «El rey está llorando y haciendo duelo por Absalón».
es.R: Alguien le dijo a Joab: «El rey está llorando y está de luto por Absalón».

fr.L: Et on rapporta à Joab : « Voici, le roi pleure, et il mène le deuil sur Absalom. »
fr.B: On vint dire à Joab : « Le roi pleure et mène le deuil sur Absalom. »
fr.R: Quelqu’un a dit à Joab : « Le roi pleure et il est en deuil à cause d’Absalom. »

vi.L: Có người báo cho Giô-áp: "Kìa, vua đang khóc và than khóc vì Áp-sa-lôm."
vi.B: Có người báo cho Giô-áp: "Vua đang khóc lóc và để tang cho Áp-sa-lôm."
vi.R: Có người báo cho Giô-áp: "Vua đang khóc và than thở vì Áp-sa-lôm."

decisions.choice: verse numbers: this is 19:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: Because the Hebrew text begins chapter 19 one verse earlier (see verse 1), this verse and every verse after it in the chapter is numbered one higher here than in many Bibles. This translation cites the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: it was told: the one who told is not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject, so the report simply reaches Joab. Joab is the man who had killed Absalom against the king's order (18:14), which gives weight to what he says next.

decisions.choice: mourning: grieving openly for the dead
decisions.reason: The verb is used of public mourning for someone who has died, as David's mourning for his son Amnon (13:37). Weeping and mourning together show grief that has taken over the king.

decisions.choice: look left out
decisions.reason: "Look" draws attention to the news. Balanced and Readable leave it out, since the report already does that work in English; Readable names an unnamed "someone" as the teller.

source.text: וַתְּהִ֨י הַתְּשֻׁעָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא לְאֵ֖בֶל לְכָל־הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֣ע הָעָ֗ם בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נֶעֱצַ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And became the victory on that day into mourning for all the people, for heard the people on that day, saying, grieved [is] the king for his son.

en.L: And the victory on that day became mourning for all the people, for the people heard on that day, saying, "The king is grieved for his son."
en.B: So the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the troops, because the troops heard it said that day, "The king is grieving over his son."
en.R: So for the whole army, the victory of that day turned into a day of sadness. The soldiers heard people say, "The king is full of grief over his son."

es.L: Y la victoria se convirtió aquel día en duelo para todo el pueblo, porque el pueblo oyó decir aquel día: «El rey está afligido por su hijo».
es.B: Así que la victoria de aquel día se convirtió en duelo para toda la tropa, porque aquel día la tropa oyó decir: «El rey está de duelo por su hijo».
es.R: Así que, para todo el ejército, la victoria de aquel día se convirtió en un día de tristeza. Los soldados oyeron que la gente decía: «El rey está muy triste por su hijo».

fr.L: Et la victoire, en ce jour-là, devint un deuil pour tout le peuple, car le peuple entendit dire ce jour-là : « Le roi est affligé à cause de son fils. »
fr.B: La victoire de ce jour se changea en deuil pour toute la troupe, car la troupe entendit dire ce jour-là : « Le roi est dans la douleur à cause de son fils. »
fr.R: Pour toute l’armée, la victoire de ce jour est devenue un jour de tristesse. Les soldats ont entendu les gens dire : « Le roi a beaucoup de chagrin à cause de son fils. »

vi.L: Chiến thắng trong ngày ấy trở thành tang chế cho toàn dân, vì trong ngày ấy dân chúng nghe nói rằng: "Vua đau buồn vì con trai mình."
vi.B: Vậy chiến thắng ngày hôm ấy biến thành ngày tang chế cho toàn quân, vì hôm ấy quân lính nghe người ta nói: "Vua đang đau buồn vì con trai mình."
vi.R: Vậy đối với cả đạo quân, chiến thắng ngày hôm ấy trở thành một ngày buồn thảm. Binh sĩ nghe người ta nói: "Vua đang rất đau buồn vì con trai mình."

decisions.choice: victory: the rescue that the battle won
decisions.reason: The word means deliverance or rescue, and it is often used of a victory that saves a people from its enemies, one that Yahweh gives (1 Samuel 11:13; 19:5). David's men had saved his kingdom and his life that day.

decisions.choice: the people: David's army
decisions.reason: "The people" here are the fighting men who had gone out against Absalom's forces (18:1-6). The word for a people is often used for a people under arms.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the army, the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the people". Balanced and Readable say who these people are, so that the reader does not think of the townspeople of Mahanaim.

source.text: וַיִּתְגַּנֵּ֥ב הָעָ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לָב֣וֹא הָעִ֑יר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְגַּנֵּ֗ב הָעָם֙ הַנִּכְלָמִ֔ים בְּנוּסָ֖ם בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And stole away the people on that day to come [into] the city, as steals away the people who are ashamed when they flee in the battle.

en.L: And the people stole away on that day to enter the city, as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
en.B: That day the troops slipped quietly into the city, the way troops creep in when they are ashamed because they have fled from battle.
en.R: That day the soldiers sneaked back into the city. They acted like soldiers who are ashamed because they ran away from a battle.

es.L: Y el pueblo entró a escondidas aquel día en la ciudad, como entra a escondidas el pueblo avergonzado cuando huye en la batalla.
es.B: Aquel día la tropa entró en la ciudad sin hacer ruido, como entra una tropa que se avergüenza por haber huido de la batalla.
es.R: Aquel día los soldados volvieron a escondidas a la ciudad. Actuaban como soldados que tienen vergüenza porque huyeron de una batalla.

fr.L: Et le peuple se glissa ce jour-là pour entrer dans la ville, comme se glisse le peuple qui a honte quand il a fui dans la bataille.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, la troupe rentra en cachette dans la ville, comme se faufilent des soldats honteux d’avoir fui le combat.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, les soldats sont rentrés dans la ville en se cachant. Ils agissaient comme des soldats qui ont honte parce qu’ils se sont enfuis pendant une bataille.

vi.L: Ngày ấy dân chúng lén lút vào thành, như dân chúng xấu hổ lén lút khi chạy trốn khỏi trận chiến.
vi.B: Hôm ấy quân lính lặng lẽ lẻn vào thành, như những người lính xấu hổ lén trở về vì đã bỏ chạy khỏi trận chiến.
vi.R: Hôm ấy binh sĩ lén lút trở vào thành. Họ giống như những người lính xấu hổ vì đã bỏ chạy khỏi trận đánh.

decisions.choice: stole away: came in secretly, as if hiding
decisions.reason: The verb is built on the word for stealing, and in this form it means to slip in or away unnoticed. The same root returns at the end of the chapter, when the men of Israel complain that Judah has "stolen" the king (verse 42).

decisions.choice: as the people who are ashamed: winners behaving like losers
decisions.reason: The comparison is pointed: the army had won, yet it came home as defeated troops do, without songs or welcome, because the king was mourning the leader of the other side.

decisions.choice: the city: Mahanaim
decisions.reason: David had taken refuge in Mahanaim, east of the Jordan, and his army marched out from its gate (17:24, 27; 18:4).

decisions.choice: slipped quietly ... creep in (Balanced); sneaked back (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use words that carry the picture of moving in secret, as the Hebrew verb does.

source.text: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לָאַ֣ט אֶת־פָּנָ֔יו וַיִּזְעַ֥ק הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל בְּנִי֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּנִ֥י בְנִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the king covered his face, and cried out the king [with] a great voice, my son Absalom, Absalom my son, my son!

en.L: And the king covered his face, and the king cried out [with] a loud voice, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"
en.B: The king covered his face and cried out in a loud voice, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"
en.R: The king covered his face and cried out loudly, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"

es.L: Y el rey se cubrió el rostro, y el rey clamaba a gran voz: «¡Mi hijo Absalón! ¡Absalón, mi hijo, mi hijo!».
es.B: El rey se cubrió la cara y gritaba a gran voz: «¡Absalón, hijo mío! ¡Absalón, hijo mío, hijo mío!».
es.R: El rey se cubrió la cara y gritaba con fuerza: «¡Absalón, hijo mío! ¡Absalón, hijo mío, hijo mío!».

fr.L: Et le roi se couvrit le visage, et le roi criait d’une voix forte : « Mon fils Absalom ! Absalom, mon fils, mon fils ! »
fr.B: Le roi se couvrit le visage et il criait d’une voix forte : « Mon fils Absalom ! Absalom, mon fils, mon fils ! »
fr.R: Le roi s’est couvert le visage et il criait très fort : « Mon fils Absalom ! Absalom, mon fils, mon fils ! »

vi.L: Vua trùm mặt lại, và vua kêu lớn tiếng: "Áp-sa-lôm con ơi! Áp-sa-lôm, con ơi, con ơi!"
vi.B: Vua trùm mặt lại và kêu lớn tiếng: "Áp-sa-lôm con ơi! Áp-sa-lôm, con ơi, con ơi!"
vi.R: Vua trùm mặt lại và kêu lớn: "Áp-sa-lôm con ơi! Áp-sa-lôm, con ơi, con ơi!"

decisions.choice: covered his face: a sign of mourning and shame
decisions.reason: Mourners covered the head or face (15:30; Jeremiah 14:3-4). The rare verb means to wrap. David hides his face from the troops who have just risked their lives for him.

decisions.choice: my son Absalom: the cry of verse 1 again
decisions.reason: The same words now reach the army outside. What the king first said in the room above the gate he now cries aloud, and this is what Joab confronts in the next verses.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א יוֹאָ֛ב אֶל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַבָּ֑יִת וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הֹבַ֨שְׁתָּ הַיּ֜וֹם אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ הַֽמְמַלְּטִ֤ים אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֵ֨ת נֶ֤פֶשׁ בָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְנֶ֣פֶשׁ נָשֶׁ֔יךָ וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ פִּלַגְשֶֽׁיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Joab to the king [into] the house, and said, you have put to shame today [the] faces of all your servants, who saved your life today and [the] life of your sons and your daughters and [the] life of your wives and [the] life of your concubines,

en.L: And Joab came to the king [into] the house and said, "You have put to shame today the faces of all your servants, who today saved your life, and the life of your sons and your daughters, and the life of your wives, and the life of your concubines,
en.B: Then Joab went in to the king in the house and said, "You have today disgraced all your servants, who this day saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, your wives and your concubines,
en.R: Then Joab went into the house where the king was. He said, "Today your men saved your life. They saved the lives of your sons and daughters, and of your wives and your concubines (secondary wives). Yet you have made all of them feel ashamed.

es.L: Y Joab entró al rey [en] la casa y dijo: «Hoy has cubierto de vergüenza el rostro de todos tus siervos, que hoy han salvado tu vida, y la vida de tus hijos y de tus hijas, y la vida de tus mujeres, y la vida de tus concubinas,
es.B: Entonces Joab entró a ver al rey en la casa y le dijo: «Hoy has avergonzado a todos tus siervos, que este día salvaron tu vida y la vida de tus hijos y tus hijas, de tus mujeres y de tus concubinas,
es.R: Entonces Joab entró en la casa donde estaba el rey. Le dijo: «Hoy tus hombres te salvaron la vida. Salvaron la vida de tus hijos y tus hijas, y de tus esposas y tus concubinas (esposas de segunda categoría). Y sin embargo, has hecho que todos ellos se sientan avergonzados.

fr.L: Et Joab vint vers le roi [dans] la maison et dit : « Tu as couvert de honte aujourd’hui le visage de tous tes serviteurs, qui ont sauvé aujourd’hui ta vie, et la vie de tes fils et de tes filles, et la vie de tes femmes, et la vie de tes concubines,
fr.B: Alors Joab entra chez le roi, dans la maison, et lui dit : « Aujourd’hui tu as couvert de honte tous tes serviteurs, eux qui ont sauvé ce jour même ta vie, celle de tes fils et de tes filles, de tes femmes et de tes concubines,
fr.R: Alors Joab est entré dans la maison où était le roi. Il lui a dit : « Aujourd’hui, tes hommes t’ont sauvé la vie. Ils ont sauvé la vie de tes fils et de tes filles, de tes femmes et de tes concubines (tes épouses de second rang). Et toi, tu leur as fait honte à tous.

vi.L: Giô-áp vào nhà gặp vua và nói: "Hôm nay vua đã làm hổ mặt tất cả các đầy tớ của vua, là những người hôm nay đã cứu mạng vua, mạng các con trai con gái vua, mạng các vợ vua và mạng các cung phi của vua,
vi.B: Bấy giờ Giô-áp vào nhà gặp vua và nói: "Hôm nay bệ hạ đã làm nhục tất cả các đầy tớ của bệ hạ, là những người hôm nay đã cứu mạng bệ hạ, mạng các hoàng tử và công chúa, các hoàng hậu và các cung phi của bệ hạ,
vi.R: Bấy giờ Giô-áp đi vào nhà nơi vua đang ở. Ông nói: "Hôm nay người của đức vua đã cứu mạng đức vua. Họ đã cứu mạng các con trai con gái của đức vua, các vợ và các cung phi (là những người vợ thứ) của đức vua. Thế mà đức vua lại làm cho tất cả họ phải xấu hổ.

decisions.choice: put to shame the faces: humiliated them openly
decisions.reason: Shame is pictured on the face, where everyone can see it. By mourning the rebel instead of thanking his rescuers, the king has disgraced them in public. The verb's form is unusual, but its sense, "put to shame", is clear from the context.

decisions.choice: your servants: the king's men, his officers and soldiers
decisions.reason: Joab uses the word that names all who serve the king, from his commanders to the fighting men who had just won the battle for him.

decisions.choice: concubines: wives of lower rank
decisions.reason: A concubine was a woman bound to a man as a secondary wife, without a free wife's full rights. Ten of David's concubines had been left in Jerusalem and taken by Absalom (15:16; 16:21-22).

decisions.choice: your men
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "your servants", as Joab speaks of the king's servants. Readable says "your men", since these are the soldiers who fought for David.

decisions.choice: the shaming put last
decisions.reason: Readable tells first what the men had done and then how the king treated them, so that a long list does not stand between the subject and the verb. It ends its own sentence here, though the Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 7, and adds "(secondary wives)" to explain "concubines".

source.text: לְאַֽהֲבָה֙ אֶת־שֹׂ֣נְאֶ֔יךָ וְלִשְׂנֹ֖א אֶת־אֹהֲבֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י׀הִגַּ֣דְתָּ הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין לְךָ֙ שָׂרִ֣ים וַעֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֣י׀יָדַ֣עְתִּי הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֠י ל֣וּ אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם חַי֙ וְכֻלָּ֤נוּ הַיּוֹם֙ מֵתִ֔ים כִּי־אָ֖ז יָשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: by loving those hating you and by hating those loving you; for you have declared today that there are not to you commanders and servants; for I know today that if Absalom [were] alive and all of us today [were] dead, that then [it would be] right in your eyes.

en.L: by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. For you have made known today that you have no commanders or servants. For I know today that if Absalom [were] alive and all of us [were] dead today, then [it would be] right in your eyes.
en.B: because you show love to those who hate you and hatred to those who love you. Today you have shown that your commanders and servants count for nothing with you. I know now that if all of us had died today and Absalom were alive, you would think it right.
en.R: You love the people who hate you, and you hate the people who love you. Today you have shown that your officers and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know now that if all of us had died today and Absalom had lived, you would have been glad.

es.L: amando a los que te odian y odiando a los que te aman. Porque hoy has dado a conocer que no tienes jefes ni siervos. Porque hoy sé que si Absalón [estuviera] vivo y todos nosotros [estuviéramos] hoy muertos, entonces [eso sería] recto a tus ojos.
es.B: porque amas a los que te odian y odias a los que te aman. Hoy has dejado ver que tus jefes y tus siervos no valen nada para ti. Ahora sé que si hoy hubiéramos muerto todos nosotros y Absalón estuviera vivo, a ti te parecería bien.
es.R: Tú amas a los que te odian, y odias a los que te aman. Hoy has mostrado que tus oficiales y tus soldados no significan nada para ti. Ahora sé que si todos nosotros hubiéramos muerto hoy y Absalón hubiera vivido, tú estarías contento.

fr.L: en aimant ceux qui te haïssent et en haïssant ceux qui t’aiment. Car tu as fait savoir aujourd’hui que tu n’as ni chefs ni serviteurs. Car je sais aujourd’hui que si Absalom [était] vivant et nous tous morts aujourd’hui, alors [ce serait] bien à tes yeux.
fr.B: car tu aimes ceux qui te haïssent et tu hais ceux qui t’aiment. Tu as montré aujourd’hui que tes chefs et tes serviteurs ne comptent pas pour toi. Je sais maintenant que si nous étions tous morts aujourd’hui et qu’Absalom était vivant, tu trouverais cela très bien.
fr.R: Tu aimes ceux qui te détestent, et tu détestes ceux qui t’aiment. Aujourd’hui, tu as montré que tes officiers et tes soldats ne comptent pas pour toi. Je le sais maintenant : si nous étions tous morts aujourd’hui et qu’Absalom était resté en vie, tu aurais été content.

vi.L: vì vua yêu những kẻ ghét vua và ghét những người yêu vua. Vì hôm nay vua đã cho thấy rằng vua không có các tướng chỉ huy hay đầy tớ. Vì hôm nay tôi biết rằng nếu Áp-sa-lôm [còn] sống và hôm nay tất cả chúng tôi [đều] chết, thì [điều đó là] đúng trong mắt vua.
vi.B: vì bệ hạ yêu những kẻ ghét mình và ghét những người yêu mình. Hôm nay bệ hạ đã cho thấy rằng các tướng chỉ huy và đầy tớ của bệ hạ chẳng là gì đối với bệ hạ. Bây giờ tôi biết rằng nếu hôm nay tất cả chúng tôi chết hết mà Áp-sa-lôm còn sống, thì bệ hạ cho là phải lẽ.
vi.R: Đức vua yêu những người ghét mình, và ghét những người yêu mình. Hôm nay đức vua đã cho thấy các tướng lĩnh và binh sĩ chẳng có nghĩa lý gì với đức vua. Bây giờ tôi biết rằng nếu hôm nay tất cả chúng tôi đều chết mà Áp-sa-lôm còn sống, thì đức vua sẽ vui lòng.

decisions.choice: by loving ... and hating: how the king has shamed his men
decisions.reason: The two infinitives explain the shaming of verse 6. Joab sharpens it into a reversal: the king treats the rebel who sought his life as one he loves, and his loyal men as people he hates.

decisions.choice: you have no commanders or servants: they mean nothing to you
decisions.reason: Joab does not mean that the king has lost his officers, but that he behaves as if they did not exist. His leaders and his men count for nothing in his eyes.

decisions.choice: right in your eyes: what you would approve of
decisions.reason: Something "right" or "good in the eyes" of a person is what that person approves or finds pleasing (verse 19; 1 Samuel 18:20). Joab's charge is bitter: the king would be content if his army had died instead of Absalom.

decisions.choice: commanders and servants (Balanced); officers and soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: A commander in a military setting stays "commander". The second word is the one used for the king's servants in verse 6; Readable says "soldiers", since Joab means the fighting men.

decisions.choice: if all of us had died today and Absalom were alive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the deaths first and Absalom's life second. The meaning is the same, and the order lets the sentence end on the king's reaction.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם צֵ֔א וְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל־לֵ֣ב עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ כִּי֩ בַיהוָ֨ה נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתִּי כִּי־אֵינְךָ֣ יוֹצֵ֗א אִם־יָלִ֨ין אִ֤ישׁ אִתְּךָ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה וְרָעָ֧ה לְךָ֣ זֹ֗את מִכָּל־הָרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣אָה עָלֶ֔יךָ מִנְּעֻרֶ֖יךָ עַד־עָֽתָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And now arise, go out and speak to [the] heart of your servants; for by Yahweh I swear that if you are not going out, not will stay a man with you this night; and this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come on you from your youth until now.

en.L: And now arise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants. For by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I swear that if you do not go out, not a man will stay the night with you tonight, and this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come on you from your youth until now."
en.B: So now get up, go out and speak to the hearts of your servants. By {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I swear: unless you go out, not a single man will spend this night with you. That would be a worse disaster for you than any that has come on you since you were young."
en.R: Now get up and go out. Speak to your men and encourage them. I make a solemn promise by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: if you do not go out, by tonight not one man will still be on your side. That would be the worst trouble you have had in your whole life."

es.L: Y ahora levántate, sal, y habla al corazón de tus siervos. Porque por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juro que si no sales, no se quedará contigo ni un hombre esta noche, y esto será peor para ti que todo el mal que te ha venido desde tu juventud hasta ahora».
es.B: Así que ahora levántate, sal y habla al corazón de tus siervos. Juro por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que, si no sales, ni un solo hombre pasará esta noche contigo. Eso sería para ti una desgracia peor que cualquiera que te haya venido desde que eras joven».
es.R: Ahora levántate y sal. Habla con tus hombres y anímalos. Te lo juro solemnemente por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: si no sales, esta noche no quedará ni un hombre de tu lado. Eso sería el peor problema que has tenido en toda tu vida».

fr.L: Et maintenant, lève-toi, sors et parle au cœur de tes serviteurs. Car je jure par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} que si tu ne sors pas, pas un homme ne passera la nuit avec toi cette nuit ; et ce sera pour toi pire que tout le mal qui t’est arrivé depuis ta jeunesse jusqu’à maintenant. »
fr.B: Lève-toi donc maintenant, sors et parle au cœur de tes serviteurs. Je le jure par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : si tu ne sors pas, pas un seul homme ne restera avec toi cette nuit. Ce serait pour toi un malheur pire que tous ceux qui te sont arrivés depuis ta jeunesse. »
fr.R: Maintenant, lève-toi et sors. Parle à tes hommes et donne-leur du courage. Je te le jure solennellement par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : si tu ne sors pas, ce soir, il ne restera plus un seul homme de ton côté. Ce serait le pire malheur de toute ta vie. »

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, vua hãy đứng dậy, đi ra và nói với lòng các đầy tớ vua. Vì tôi nhân danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà thề rằng, nếu vua không đi ra, thì đêm nay sẽ không một người nào ở lại với vua; và điều ấy sẽ tệ hại cho vua hơn mọi tai họa đã đến trên vua từ thuở nhỏ cho đến bây giờ."
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ bệ hạ hãy đứng dậy, đi ra và nói lời an ủi các đầy tớ của bệ hạ. Tôi xin nhân danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà thề: nếu bệ hạ không ra, thì đêm nay sẽ không còn một ai ở lại với bệ hạ. Điều đó sẽ là tai họa tồi tệ hơn mọi tai họa bệ hạ đã gặp từ thuở thiếu thời đến nay."
vi.R: Bây giờ đức vua hãy đứng dậy đi ra. Hãy nói chuyện với người của đức vua và khích lệ họ. Tôi xin nhân danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà thề: nếu đức vua không ra, thì đến tối nay sẽ không còn một ai đứng về phía đức vua nữa. Đó sẽ là tai họa tồi tệ nhất trong cả cuộc đời đức vua."

decisions.choice: speak to the heart: speak kindly, to reassure and encourage
decisions.reason: To speak "to the heart" of someone is to speak words that comfort and win them, as Joseph did with his brothers (Genesis 50:21) and Boaz with Ruth (Ruth 2:13).

decisions.choice: if you do not go out, not a man will stay: an oath that none will remain
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if ... (then may it be so)" is a firm denial: Joab swears by Yahweh that, unless the king appears, every man will be gone by morning.

decisions.choice: stay the night: remain with him, stay loyal
decisions.reason: The verb means to spend the night. Here it means that by the next morning the king would find his army had deserted him.

decisions.choice: your men
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, Literal and Balanced keep "your servants" and Readable says "your men".

decisions.choice: I make a solemn promise by the LORD; still be on your side
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what an oath is and that staying means staying loyal. It turns "all the evil from your youth until now" into "the worst trouble ... in your whole life".

source.text: וַיָּ֥קָם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בַּשָּׁ֑עַר וּֽלְכָל־הָעָ֞ם הִגִּ֣ידוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֤ה הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיָּבֹ֤א כָל־הָעָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נָ֖ס אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And arose the king and sat in the gate; and to all the people they told, saying, look, the king [is] sitting in the gate; and came all the people before the king. And Israel had fled, each to his tents.

en.L: And the king arose and sat in the gate. And they told all the people, saying, "Look, the king [is] sitting in the gate." And all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled, each to his tents.
en.B: So the king got up and took his seat in the gate. All the troops were told, "The king is sitting in the gate," and they all came into his presence. As for Israel, they had fled, each man to his home.
en.R: So the king got up and sat down at the city gate. All the soldiers were told, "The king is sitting at the gate." Then they all came to see him. Meanwhile, the Israelites who had followed Absalom had all run away to their homes.

es.L: Y el rey se levantó y se sentó en la puerta. Y se lo anunciaron a todo el pueblo, diciendo: «He aquí, el rey [está] sentado en la puerta». Y todo el pueblo vino delante del rey. Pero Israel había huido, cada uno a sus tiendas.
es.B: Entonces el rey se levantó y se sentó en la puerta. A toda la tropa le avisaron: «El rey está sentado en la puerta», y todos vinieron a presentarse ante él. En cuanto a Israel, habían huido, cada uno a su casa.
es.R: Entonces el rey se levantó y se sentó en la puerta de la ciudad. A todos los soldados les avisaron: «El rey está sentado en la puerta». Entonces todos vinieron a verlo. Mientras tanto, los israelitas que habían seguido a Absalón se habían ido corriendo a sus casas.

fr.L: Et le roi se leva et s’assit à la porte. Et on l’annonça à tout le peuple, disant : « Voici, le roi est assis à la porte. » Et tout le peuple vint devant le roi. Or Israël s’était enfui, chacun à ses tentes.
fr.B: Le roi se leva donc et prit place à la porte. On l’annonça à toute la troupe : « Le roi siège à la porte », et tous vinrent se présenter devant lui. Quant à Israël, il s’était enfui, chacun chez soi.
fr.R: Le roi s’est donc levé et il s’est assis à la porte de la ville. On a dit à tous les soldats : « Le roi est assis à la porte. » Alors ils sont tous venus le voir. Pendant ce temps, les Israélites qui avaient suivi Absalom s’étaient tous enfuis chez eux.

vi.L: Vua đứng dậy và ngồi tại cổng thành. Người ta báo cho toàn dân rằng: "Kìa, vua đang ngồi tại cổng thành." Toàn dân đến trước mặt vua. Còn Y-sơ-ra-ên đã chạy trốn, ai về trại nấy.
vi.B: Vậy vua đứng dậy ra ngồi tại cổng thành. Người ta báo cho toàn quân: "Vua đang ngồi tại cổng thành," và tất cả đều đến trước mặt vua. Còn người Y-sơ-ra-ên thì đã chạy trốn, ai về nhà nấy.
vi.R: Vậy vua đứng dậy và ra ngồi ở cổng thành. Người ta báo cho tất cả binh sĩ: "Vua đang ngồi ở cổng thành." Rồi tất cả họ đến gặp vua. Trong khi đó, những người Y-sơ-ra-ên đã theo Áp-sa-lôm đều đã chạy trốn về nhà mình.

decisions.choice: sat in the gate: took his place where the king met his people
decisions.reason: The gate was the town's public meeting place, where kings and elders sat to hear the people and give judgment (15:2; 18:4; Ruth 4:1). By sitting there the king shows himself to the army as its king again.

decisions.choice: Israel had fled: Absalom's army, scattered after the battle
decisions.reason: The clause turns to the other side: the men of Israel who had followed Absalom had fled home (18:17). It also opens the next scene, in which the tribes argue about bringing David back.

decisions.choice: each to his tents: each man to his home
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Israel's early life in tents and means going home (18:17; 20:1; 1 Kings 12:16).

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3. Balanced says "the Israelites" and "his home" to make the idiom of meaning decision m3 plain.

decisions.choice: who had followed Absalom
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "Israel" here means Absalom's side, not David's army.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י כָל־הָעָם֙ נָד֔וֹן בְּכָל־שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ הִצִּילָ֣נוּ׀מִכַּ֣ף אֹיְבֵ֗ינוּ וְה֤וּא מִלְּטָ֨נוּ֙ מִכַּ֣ף פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַתָּ֛ה בָּרַ֥ח מִן־הָאָ֖רֶץ מֵעַ֥ל אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the people were arguing in all [the] tribes of Israel, saying, the king delivered us from [the] palm of our enemies, and he rescued us from [the] palm of [the] Philistines, and now he has fled from the land from Absalom.

en.L: And all the people were arguing throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies, and he rescued us from the hand of the Philistines, and now he has fled out of the land from Absalom.
en.B: Throughout all the tribes of Israel the people were arguing with one another. "The king rescued us from the power of our enemies," they said. "He saved us from the power of the Philistines. Yet now he has fled out of the land because of Absalom.
en.R: All through the tribes of Israel, people were arguing with one another. They said, "The king rescued us from our enemies. He saved us from the Philistines. But now he has run away from the country because of Absalom.

es.L: Y todo el pueblo discutía en todas las tribus de Israel, diciendo: «El rey nos libró de la mano de nuestros enemigos, y nos rescató de la mano de los filisteos, y ahora ha huido del país por causa de Absalón.
es.B: Por todas las tribus de Israel la gente discutía entre sí. Decían: «El rey nos libró del poder de nuestros enemigos. Nos salvó del poder de los filisteos. Pero ahora ha huido del país por causa de Absalón.
es.R: Por todas las tribus de Israel, la gente discutía entre sí. Decían: «El rey nos libró de nuestros enemigos. Nos salvó de los filisteos. Pero ahora ha huido del país por causa de Absalón.

fr.L: Et tout le peuple se disputait dans toutes les tribus d’Israël, disant : « Le roi nous a délivrés de la main de nos ennemis, et c’est lui qui nous a sauvés de la main des Philistins ; et maintenant il a fui hors du pays à cause d’Absalom.
fr.B: Dans toutes les tribus d’Israël, le peuple se disputait. « Le roi nous a délivrés du pouvoir de nos ennemis, disait-on. Il nous a sauvés du pouvoir des Philistins. Et maintenant, il a fui hors du pays à cause d’Absalom.
fr.R: Dans toutes les tribus d’Israël, les gens se disputaient. Ils disaient : « Le roi nous a délivrés de nos ennemis. Il nous a sauvés des Philistins. Mais maintenant, il s’est enfui du pays à cause d’Absalom.

vi.L: Toàn dân trong khắp các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên đều tranh cãi với nhau rằng: "Vua đã giải cứu chúng ta khỏi lòng bàn tay của kẻ thù, và đã cứu chúng ta khỏi lòng bàn tay người Phi-li-tin; nhưng bây giờ vua đã chạy trốn khỏi xứ vì Áp-sa-lôm.
vi.B: Trong khắp các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên, dân chúng tranh cãi với nhau. Họ nói: "Vua đã giải cứu chúng ta khỏi quyền lực của kẻ thù. Vua đã cứu chúng ta khỏi quyền lực của người Phi-li-tin. Thế mà bây giờ vua phải chạy trốn khỏi xứ vì Áp-sa-lôm.
vi.R: Khắp các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên, người ta tranh cãi với nhau. Họ nói: "Vua đã giải cứu chúng ta khỏi kẻ thù. Vua đã cứu chúng ta khỏi người Phi-li-tin. Nhưng bây giờ vua phải chạy trốn khỏi xứ vì Áp-sa-lôm.

decisions.choice: arguing: disputing among themselves
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of the word for judging or pleading a case. The tribes are divided and debating what to do now that the king they had chosen is dead.

decisions.choice: the palm of our enemies: the power of our enemies
decisions.reason: The hand or palm stands for power and control. To be rescued from someone's hand is to be freed from their grip.

decisions.choice: from the hand of the Philistines: David's victories
decisions.reason: David had first won Israel's love by defeating the Philistines (1 Samuel 17-18), and as king he broke their power over the land (5:17-25; 8:1).

decisions.choice: the power of (Balanced); left out (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "hand" into "power". Readable simply says "rescued us from our enemies", which carries the sense.

source.text: וְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָשַׁ֣חְנוּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ מֵ֖ת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֗ה לָמָ֥ה אַתֶּ֛ם מַחֲרִשִׁ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in the battle; and now why [are] you keeping silent to bring back the king?

en.L: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in the battle. And now, why [are] you keeping silent about bringing back the king?"
en.B: And Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, has died in battle. So now, why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"
en.R: We anointed Absalom to be king over us, but he has died in the battle. So why is no one saying anything about bringing King David back?"

es.L: Y Absalón, a quien ungimos sobre nosotros, ha muerto en la batalla. Y ahora, ¿por qué {{plural_you:callan|calláis}} en cuanto a hacer volver al rey?».
es.B: Y Absalón, a quien ungimos para que nos gobernara, ha muerto en la batalla. Entonces, ¿por qué no {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} nada de hacer volver al rey?».
es.R: Ungimos a Absalón como rey sobre nosotros, pero ha muerto en la batalla. Entonces, ¿por qué nadie dice nada de traer de vuelta al rey David?».

fr.L: Et Absalom, que nous avions oint sur nous, est mort dans la bataille. Et maintenant, pourquoi gardez-vous le silence pour ramener le roi ? »
fr.B: Et Absalom, que nous avions oint pour régner sur nous, est mort au combat. Alors pourquoi ne dites-vous rien pour faire revenir le roi ? »
fr.R: Nous avions oint Absalom pour qu’il soit notre roi, mais il est mort dans la bataille. Alors pourquoi personne ne parle-t-il de ramener le roi David ? »

vi.L: Còn Áp-sa-lôm, người mà chúng ta đã xức dầu [làm vua] trên chúng ta, đã chết trong trận chiến. Vậy bây giờ, sao các ông cứ im lặng không đem vua trở về?"
vi.B: Còn Áp-sa-lôm, người chúng ta đã xức dầu để cai trị chúng ta, thì đã chết trận. Vậy bây giờ sao các ông chẳng nói gì đến việc đưa vua trở về?"
vi.R: Chúng ta đã xức dầu cho Áp-sa-lôm làm vua, nhưng chàng đã chết trận. Vậy sao không ai nói gì đến việc đưa vua Đa-vít trở về?"

decisions.choice: whom we anointed over us: whom we made king
decisions.reason: Pouring oil on a man's head set him apart as king (2:4; 5:3). Absalom had been proclaimed king at Hebron (15:10), and now the men of Israel admit that they chose him.

decisions.choice: you: the people of the tribes, speaking to one another
decisions.reason: The pronoun is plural. The tribes press their own leaders, and one another, to act.

decisions.choice: King David
decisions.reason: Readable names the king, since Absalom was called king too.

source.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד שָׁ֠לַח אֶל־צָד֨וֹק וְאֶל־אֶבְיָתָ֥ר הַכֹּהֲנִים֮ לֵאמֹר֒ דַּבְּר֞וּ אֶל־זִקְנֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיוּ֙ אַֽחֲרֹנִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ וּדְבַר֙ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֥א אֶל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, speak to [the] elders of Judah, saying, why will you be last to bring back the king to his house? And [the] word of all Israel has come to the king, to his house.

en.L: And King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house, when the word of all Israel has come to the king, to his house?
en.B: King David sent this message to the priests Zadok and Abiathar: "Ask the elders of Judah, 'Why should you be last of all in bringing the king back to his palace? What all Israel is saying has reached the king in his house.
en.R: King David sent a message to the priests Zadok and Abiathar. It said, "Speak to the leaders of Judah. Ask them, 'Why should you be the last ones to bring the king back to his palace? The king has heard what the people all over Israel are saying.

es.L: Y el rey David envió a decir a Sadoc y a Abiatar los sacerdotes: «{{plural_you:Hablen|Hablad}} a los ancianos de Judá, diciendo: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los últimos en hacer volver al rey a su casa, cuando la palabra de todo Israel ha llegado al rey, a su casa?
es.B: El rey David les envió este mensaje a los sacerdotes Sadoc y Abiatar: «{{plural_you:Pregúntenles|Preguntadles}} a los ancianos de Judá: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:han|habéis}} de ser {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los últimos en hacer volver al rey a su palacio? Lo que dice todo Israel ha llegado ya al rey en su casa.
es.R: El rey David les envió un mensaje a los sacerdotes Sadoc y Abiatar. Decía: «{{plural_you:Hablen|Hablad}} con los líderes de Judá. {{plural_you:Pregúntenles|Preguntadles}}: “¿Por qué {{plural_you:han|habéis}} de ser {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los últimos en traer al rey de vuelta a su palacio? El rey ya ha oído lo que dice la gente en todo Israel.

fr.L: Et le roi David envoya [dire] aux prêtres Sadok et Abiathar : « Parlez aux anciens de Juda, disant : “Pourquoi seriez-vous les derniers à ramener le roi dans sa maison, alors que la parole de tout Israël est parvenue au roi, jusqu’à sa maison ?
fr.B: Le roi David fit dire aux prêtres Sadok et Abiathar : « Demandez aux anciens de Juda : “Pourquoi seriez-vous les derniers à ramener le roi dans son palais ? Ce que dit tout Israël est déjà parvenu jusqu’au roi, dans sa maison.
fr.R: Le roi David a envoyé un message aux prêtres Sadok et Abiathar. Il disait : « Parlez aux responsables de Juda. Demandez-leur : “Pourquoi seriez-vous les derniers à ramener le roi dans son palais ? Le roi sait déjà ce que disent les gens dans tout Israël.

vi.L: Vua Đa-vít sai người đến nói với các thầy tế lễ Xa-đốc và A-bi-a-tha rằng: "Hãy nói với các trưởng lão Giu-đa rằng: 'Sao các ông lại là những người sau cùng đem vua về cung, khi lời của cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đã đến tai vua, tại cung vua?
vi.B: Vua Đa-vít gửi lời nhắn đến các thầy tế lễ Xa-đốc và A-bi-a-tha: "Hãy hỏi các trưởng lão Giu-đa: 'Sao các ông lại là những người sau cùng đưa vua về cung? Những điều cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đang nói đã đến tai vua trong cung rồi.
vi.R: Vua Đa-vít gửi một lời nhắn cho các thầy tế lễ Xa-đốc và A-bi-a-tha. Lời nhắn như sau: "Hãy nói với những người lãnh đạo Giu-đa. Hãy hỏi họ: 'Sao các ông lại là những người sau cùng đưa vua về cung? Vua đã nghe điều mà dân chúng khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên đang nói.

decisions.choice: the word of all Israel has come to the king: part of the message to Judah
alternatives: a narrator's note: the talk of all Israel had reached the king
placed at the end of verse 11 (Greek)
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text this clause stands at the end of the verse, after the question. This translation takes it as part of the message: the other tribes are already talking of bringing David back, so Judah is in danger of being last. It could also be a note from the narrator explaining why David sent the message. The ancient Greek translation places it at the end of verse 11 instead.

decisions.choice: the elders of Judah: the leaders of David's own tribe
decisions.reason: Judah was David's tribe, and Hebron in Judah was where Absalom's revolt began (15:7-12). Its leaders may have hung back from fear of what David would do to them.

decisions.choice: his house: the king's palace in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "House" here is the royal residence. In the second clause "to his house" may mean where the king was staying, at Mahanaim.

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the first "house", since the king's home in Jerusalem is meant.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", the older men who led the tribe.

source.text: אַחַ֣י אַתֶּ֔ם עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אַתֶּ֑ם וְלָ֧מָּה תִהְי֛וּ אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: My brothers [are] you; my bone and my flesh [are] you; and why will you be last to bring back the king?

en.L: You [are] my brothers; my bone and my flesh [are] you. And why should you be the last to bring back the king?'
en.B: You are my brothers; you are my own bone and flesh. Why then should you be last of all in bringing the king back?'
en.R: You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be last of all in bringing the king back?'

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} [son] mis hermanos; mi hueso y mi carne [son] {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¿Por qué, pues, {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} los últimos en hacer volver al rey?”.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:son|sois}} mis hermanos; {{plural_you:son|sois}} mi propio hueso y mi propia carne. ¿Por qué, entonces, {{plural_you:han|habéis}} de ser los últimos en hacer volver al rey?”.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:son|sois}} mis parientes, de mi propia sangre. Entonces, ¿por qué {{plural_you:han|habéis}} de ser los últimos en traer de vuelta al rey?”.

fr.L: Vous [êtes] mes frères ; vous [êtes] mes os et ma chair. Et pourquoi seriez-vous les derniers à ramener le roi ?”
fr.B: Vous êtes mes frères, vous êtes de mes os et de ma chair. Pourquoi donc seriez-vous les derniers à ramener le roi ?”
fr.R: Vous êtes ma famille, de mon sang. Alors pourquoi seriez-vous les derniers à ramener le roi ?”

vi.L: Các ông [là] anh em của ta; các ông [là] xương ta và thịt ta. Sao các ông lại là những người sau cùng đem vua trở về?'
vi.B: Các ông là anh em của ta, là cốt nhục của ta. Vậy sao các ông lại là những người sau cùng đưa vua trở về?'
vi.R: Các ông là bà con của ta, là ruột thịt của ta. Vậy sao các ông lại là những người sau cùng đưa vua trở về?'

decisions.choice: my bone and my flesh: my own close kin
decisions.reason: The phrase names people of one family or blood (Genesis 2:23; 29:14). The tribes of Israel used it of David when they made him king (5:1); now David uses it to call Judah back to him.

decisions.choice: my brothers: fellow members of my tribe
decisions.reason: "Brothers" covers relatives and fellow tribesmen. David is of the tribe of Judah, and he appeals to that bond.

decisions.choice: my own flesh and blood
decisions.reason: Readable uses the familiar English phrase for close family in place of "bone and flesh"; Balanced keeps the Hebrew picture.

source.text: וְלַֽעֲמָשָׂא֙ תֹּֽמְר֔וּ הֲל֛וֹא עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף אִם־לֹ֠א שַׂר־צָבָ֞א תִּהְיֶ֧ה לְפָנַ֛י כָּל־הַיָּמִ֖ים תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Amasa you will say, [are] not my bone and my flesh you? Thus may do to me God, and thus may he add, if not commander of [the] army you will be before me all the days in place of Joab.

en.L: And to Amasa you shall say, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? Thus may God do to me, and thus may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add, if you are not commander of the army before me all the days in place of Joab.'"
en.B: And say to Amasa, 'Are you not my own bone and flesh? May God deal with me ever so severely if you do not become commander of my army from now on in place of Joab.'"
en.R: And tell Amasa, 'You are my own flesh and blood. From now on you will be the commander of my army instead of Joab. If I do not do this, may God punish me terribly.'"

es.L: Y a Amasa le {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “¿No [eres] tú mi hueso y mi carne? Así me haga Dios, y aun me añada, si no eres jefe del ejército delante de mí todos los días en lugar de Joab”».
es.B: Y {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}} a Amasa: “¿No eres tú mi propio hueso y mi propia carne? Que Dios me castigue, y aun más, si de ahora en adelante no eres el jefe de mi ejército en lugar de Joab”».
es.R: Y {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}} a Amasa: “Tú eres de mi propia sangre. De ahora en adelante serás el jefe de mi ejército en lugar de Joab. Si no lo hago, que Dios me castigue duramente”».

fr.L: Et à Amasa vous direz : “N’es-tu pas mes os et ma chair ? Que Dieu me fasse ainsi, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y ajoute encore, si tu n’es pas devant moi chef de l’armée pour toujours, à la place de Joab !” »
fr.B: Et dites à Amasa : “N’es-tu pas de mes os et de ma chair ? Que Dieu me traite avec sévérité et plus encore, si tu ne deviens pas dès maintenant le chef de mon armée à la place de Joab !” »
fr.R: Et dites à Amasa : “Tu es de ma famille, de mon sang. À partir de maintenant, tu seras le chef de mon armée à la place de Joab. Si je ne le fais pas, que Dieu me punisse sévèrement !” »

vi.L: Còn với A-ma-sa, các ông hãy nói: 'Chẳng phải ngươi là xương ta và thịt ta sao? Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời làm như vậy cho ta, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn thêm nữa, nếu ngươi không làm tướng chỉ huy quân đội trước mặt ta suốt đời, thay cho Giô-áp.'"
vi.B: Và hãy nói với A-ma-sa: 'Chẳng phải ngươi là cốt nhục của ta sao? Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời phạt ta thật nặng nề nếu từ nay ngươi không làm tướng chỉ huy quân đội của ta thay cho Giô-áp.'"
vi.R: Và hãy nói với A-ma-sa: 'Ngươi là ruột thịt của ta. Từ nay ngươi sẽ làm tướng chỉ huy quân đội của ta thay cho Giô-áp. Nếu ta không làm như vậy, nguyện Đức Chúa Trời phạt ta thật nặng.'"

decisions.choice: Amasa: Absalom's commander, and David's nephew
decisions.reason: Absalom had made Amasa commander of his army in place of Joab (17:25). He was a son of Abigail, David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16-17), and so a cousin of Joab; David can call him his own bone and flesh.

decisions.choice: thus may God do to me, and thus may he add: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: The speaker calls on God to punish him severely if he does not keep his word (1 Samuel 3:17; 2 Samuel 3:9, 35). The punishment is left unspoken.

decisions.choice: commander of the army in place of Joab: a bid for the rebels' loyalty
decisions.reason: By giving the rebel commander Joab's post, David offers the men who had followed Absalom a sign that they will not be punished. He also removes Joab, who had killed Absalom against his order (18:5, 14). The step costs Amasa his life (20:8-10).

decisions.choice: before me all the days: in my service for good
decisions.reason: To stand "before" the king is to serve him; "all the days" means from now on, as long as he lives.

decisions.choice: May God deal with me ever so severely (Balanced); may God punish me terribly (Readable)
decisions.reason: The oath is worded as in 3:9 and 3:35. Readable puts the promise first and the oath after it, so that the reader knows what is being sworn before hearing the curse.

decisions.choice: "Que Dieu me fasse ainsi, et qu’il y ajoute encore" (L); "Que Dieu me traite avec sévérité et plus encore" (B); "que Dieu me punisse sévèrement" (R)
alternatives: "Que Dieu me punisse" at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the words of the oath (m2); Balanced uses the oath formula of the Samuel terms note; Readable says plainly what is called down. At Literal the free pronoun for God takes the deity_pronoun span, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Así me haga Dios, y aun me añada (L); Que Dios me castigue, y aun más (B); que Dios me castigue duramente (R)
decisions.reason: The oath formula: Literal keeps the Hebrew 'thus may God do to me and thus may he add'; Balanced uses the terms note's 'Que Dios me castigue, y aun más'; Readable puts the condition first and the oath after, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời làm như vậy cho ta, và Ngài còn thêm nữa" (L); "Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời phạt ta thật nặng nề" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the oath formula; Balanced and Readable follow the Samuel terms note's "Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời phạt ... nặng nề", with "ta" in the king's mouth.

source.text: וַיַּ֛ט אֶת־לְבַ֥ב כָּל־אִישׁ־יְהוּדָ֖ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שׁ֥וּב אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל־עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he turned [the] heart of all [the] men of Judah like one man; and they sent to the king, return, you and all your servants.

en.L: And he turned the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, and they sent to the king, "Return, you and all your servants."
en.B: So he won over the hearts of all the men of Judah as if they were one man, and they sent word to the king: "Come back, you and all your officials."
en.R: In this way all the men of Judah were won over, and they all agreed together. They sent this message to the king: "Come back, you and all your officials."

es.L: Y él inclinó el corazón de todos los hombres de Judá como un solo hombre, y enviaron a decir al rey: «Vuelve, tú y todos tus siervos».
es.B: Así se ganó el corazón de todos los hombres de Judá, como si fueran un solo hombre, y le mandaron decir al rey: «Vuelve, tú y todos tus oficiales».
es.R: De esta manera se ganó a todos los hombres de Judá, y todos se pusieron de acuerdo. Le enviaron al rey este mensaje: «Vuelve, tú y todos tus oficiales».

fr.L: Et il inclina le cœur de tous les hommes de Juda comme un seul homme, et ils envoyèrent [dire] au roi : « Reviens, toi et tous tes serviteurs. »
fr.B: Il gagna ainsi le cœur de tous les hommes de Juda, comme s’ils n’étaient qu’un seul homme, et ils envoyèrent dire au roi : « Reviens, toi et tous tes officiers. »
fr.R: C’est ainsi que tous les hommes de Juda ont été gagnés, et ils étaient tous d’accord. Ils ont envoyé ce message au roi : « Reviens, toi et tous tes officiers. »

vi.L: Ông làm cho lòng mọi người Giu-đa xoay về như một người, và họ sai người đến nói với vua: "Xin vua trở về, vua và tất cả các đầy tớ của vua."
vi.B: Như vậy ông đã chinh phục được lòng mọi người Giu-đa, khiến họ đồng lòng như một người. Họ gửi lời đến vua: "Xin bệ hạ trở về cùng tất cả quần thần."
vi.R: Bằng cách ấy, mọi người Giu-đa đều được thuyết phục, và họ đồng lòng với nhau. Họ gửi lời nhắn cho vua: "Xin đức vua trở về cùng tất cả quần thần."

decisions.choice: he turned: David, through his message, or Amasa
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. The most natural subject is David, whose appeal (verses 12-14) won Judah over. It could also be Amasa, whom David has just promised to make commander.

decisions.choice: as one man: all together, with one mind
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a whole group acting in full agreement (Judges 20:1, 8, 11).

decisions.choice: your servants: the king's household and officials
decisions.reason: Here the word names those who had gone into exile with the king, his court and household.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "servants". Balanced and Readable say "officials" for the king's court.

decisions.choice: all the men of Judah were won over
decisions.reason: Readable puts the verb in the passive so that it does not choose between the two subjects in meaning decision m1.

source.text: וַיָּ֣שָׁב הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וִיהוּדָ֞ה בָּ֣א הַגִּלְגָּ֗לָה לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהַעֲבִ֥יר אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned the king and came to the Jordan; and Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.

en.L: And the king returned and came to the Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.
en.B: So the king started back and came as far as the Jordan. Judah had come to Gilgal to meet the king and to bring him across the Jordan.
en.R: So the king started back home and reached the Jordan River. The people of Judah had come to Gilgal to meet the king and help him cross the river.

es.L: Y el rey volvió y llegó al Jordán. Y Judá vino a Gilgal para ir al encuentro del rey, para hacer pasar al rey el Jordán.
es.B: Así que el rey emprendió el regreso y llegó hasta el Jordán. Judá había venido a Gilgal para recibir al rey y ayudarlo a cruzar el Jordán.
es.R: Así que el rey emprendió el regreso a casa y llegó al río Jordán. La gente de Judá había venido a Gilgal para recibir al rey y ayudarlo a cruzar el río.

fr.L: Et le roi revint et arriva au Jourdain ; et Juda vint à Guilgal pour aller à la rencontre du roi, pour faire passer le Jourdain au roi.
fr.B: Le roi prit le chemin du retour et arriva au Jourdain. Juda était venu à Guilgal pour aller à la rencontre du roi et lui faire passer le Jourdain.
fr.R: Le roi est donc reparti vers chez lui et il est arrivé au Jourdain. Les gens de Juda étaient venus à Guilgal pour accueillir le roi et l’aider à traverser le fleuve.

vi.L: Vua trở về và đến sông Giô-đanh. Giu-đa đến Ghinh-ganh để đi đón vua, để đưa vua qua sông Giô-đanh.
vi.B: Vậy vua lên đường trở về và đến sông Giô-đanh. Người Giu-đa đã đến Ghinh-ganh để đón vua và đưa vua qua sông Giô-đanh.
vi.R: Vậy vua lên đường trở về và đến sông Giô-đanh. Người Giu-đa đã đến Ghinh-ganh để đón vua và giúp vua qua sông.

decisions.choice: Gilgal: near Jericho, west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilgal was Israel's first camp in the land after crossing the Jordan (Joshua 4:19-20), and Saul's kingship was renewed there (1 Samuel 11:14-15). The tribe of Judah meets David on the bank he will cross to.

decisions.choice: Judah: the men of the tribe of Judah
decisions.reason: The tribe's name stands for its people; verse 17 calls them "the men of Judah".

decisions.choice: River; the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" the first time the Jordan is named in the chapter, and says "the people of Judah" for the tribe's name.

source.text: וַיְמַהֵ֗ר שִׁמְעִ֤י בֶן־גֵּרָא֙ בֶּן־הַיְמִינִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִבַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֨רֶד֙ עִם־אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה לִקְרַ֖את הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And hurried Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite, who [was] from Bahurim, and came down with [the] men of Judah to meet King David.

en.L: And Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite who [was] from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
en.B: Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, came down in haste with the men of Judah to meet King David.
en.R: Shimei son of Gera hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David. Shimei belonged to the tribe of Benjamin and lived in Bahurim.

es.L: Y Simei hijo de Gera, el benjamita que [era] de Bahurim, se dio prisa y bajó con los hombres de Judá al encuentro del rey David.
es.B: Simei hijo de Gera, el benjamita de Bahurim, bajó apresuradamente con los hombres de Judá a recibir al rey David.
es.R: Simei hijo de Gera bajó de prisa con los hombres de Judá a recibir al rey David. Simei era de la tribu de Benjamín y vivía en Bahurim.

fr.L: Et Shiméï, fils de Guéra, le Benjaminite, qui [était] de Bahourim, se hâta et descendit avec les hommes de Juda à la rencontre du roi David.
fr.B: Shiméï, fils de Guéra, le Benjaminite de Bahourim, se hâta de descendre avec les hommes de Juda à la rencontre du roi David.
fr.R: Shiméï, fils de Guéra, s’est dépêché de descendre avec les hommes de Juda pour accueillir le roi David. Shiméï était de la tribu de Benjamin et il habitait à Bahourim.

vi.L: Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra, người Bên-gia-min ở Ba-hu-rim, vội vã đi xuống cùng với người Giu-đa để đón vua Đa-vít.
vi.B: Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra, người Bên-gia-min ở Ba-hu-rim, vội vàng đi xuống cùng với người Giu-đa để đón vua Đa-vít.
vi.R: Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra vội vàng đi xuống cùng với người Giu-đa để đón vua Đa-vít. Si-mê-i thuộc chi tộc Bên-gia-min và sống ở Ba-hu-rim.

decisions.choice: Shimei: the man who cursed David as he fled
decisions.reason: At Bahurim Shimei had thrown stones at David, cursed him and called him a man of blood, saying that Yahweh was paying him back for the house of Saul (16:5-13). Now he hurries to be among the first to welcome David back.

decisions.choice: the Benjaminite from Bahurim: from Saul's tribe
decisions.reason: Bahurim was a village in Benjamin, just east of Jerusalem. Benjamin was Saul's tribe, and Shimei was of Saul's clan (16:5).

decisions.choice: a separate sentence on Benjamin and Bahurim
decisions.reason: Readable moves the description of Shimei to a sentence of its own and explains "Benjaminite".

source.text: וְאֶ֨לֶף אִ֣ישׁ עִמּוֹ֮ מִבִּנְיָמִן֒ וְצִיבָ֗א נַ֚עַר בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וַחֲמֵ֨שֶׁת עָשָׂ֥ר בָּנָ֛יו וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ וְצָלְח֥וּ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And a thousand men [were] with him from Benjamin, and Ziba [the] attendant of [the] house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty slaves with him; and they rushed [to] the Jordan before the king.

en.L: And a thousand men from Benjamin [were] with him, and Ziba the attendant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty slaves [were] with him. And they rushed [to] the Jordan before the king.
en.B: With him were a thousand men from Benjamin, and Ziba the attendant of Saul's household, with his fifteen sons and his twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan ahead of the king.
en.R: A thousand men from the tribe of Benjamin came with Shimei. Ziba, who had served Saul's family, came too, with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They all hurried down to the Jordan to get there before the king.

es.L: Y con él [venían] mil hombres de Benjamín, y Siba el servidor de la casa de Saúl, y sus quince hijos y sus veinte esclavos con él. Y se lanzaron [al] Jordán delante del rey.
es.B: Con él venían mil hombres de Benjamín, y Siba, el servidor de la casa de Saúl, con sus quince hijos y sus veinte siervos. Bajaron de prisa al Jordán antes que el rey.
es.R: Mil hombres de la tribu de Benjamín vinieron con Simei. También vino Siba, que había servido a la familia de Saúl, con sus quince hijos y veinte siervos. Todos bajaron de prisa al Jordán para llegar antes que el rey.

fr.L: Et mille hommes de Benjamin [étaient] avec lui, et Tsiba, le serviteur de la maison de Saül, et ses quinze fils et ses vingt esclaves [étaient] avec lui. Et ils se précipitèrent [vers] le Jourdain devant le roi.
fr.B: Il avait avec lui mille hommes de Benjamin, ainsi que Tsiba, l’intendant de la maison de Saül, avec ses quinze fils et ses vingt serviteurs. Ils se précipitèrent vers le Jourdain avant le roi.
fr.R: Mille hommes de la tribu de Benjamin étaient venus avec Shiméï. Tsiba, qui avait servi la famille de Saül, était venu aussi, avec ses quinze fils et ses vingt serviteurs. Ils se sont tous dépêchés de descendre au Jourdain pour y arriver avant le roi.

vi.L: Có một nghìn người Bên-gia-min [đi] với ông, và Xíp-ba, quản gia nhà Sau-lơ, cùng mười lăm con trai và hai mươi nô lệ của ông [đi] với ông. Họ lao xuống sông Giô-đanh trước mặt vua.
vi.B: Cùng đi với ông có một nghìn người Bên-gia-min, và Xíp-ba, quản gia nhà Sau-lơ, với mười lăm con trai và hai mươi đầy tớ của ông. Họ vội vã xuống sông Giô-đanh trước khi vua đến.
vi.R: Có một nghìn người thuộc chi tộc Bên-gia-min đi với Si-mê-i. Xíp-ba, người từng phục vụ gia đình Sau-lơ, cũng đến cùng với mười lăm con trai và hai mươi đầy tớ của ông. Tất cả đều vội vã xuống sông Giô-đanh để đến đó trước vua.

decisions.choice: a thousand men from Benjamin: Saul's tribe comes to make peace
decisions.reason: Benjamin had most reason to fear David's return, since it was Saul's tribe and Shimei had cursed David. A large company from it comes out to show its loyalty.

decisions.choice: Ziba: the steward of Saul's estate
decisions.reason: David had put Ziba in charge of the land he gave Mephibosheth (9:9-10). When David fled, Ziba met him with supplies and accused his master of hoping to gain the throne, and David gave him everything that had been Mephibosheth's (16:1-4).

decisions.choice: rushed to the Jordan before the king: hurried down to reach it ahead of him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of something rushing on or plunging forward. They went down to the river ahead of the king, perhaps into its waters, to be there to serve him when he crossed.

decisions.choice: attendant (Literal, Balanced); slaves (Literal), servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Ziba's title is the word used of him in 9:9, rendered "attendant" there. His own workers are "slaves" at Literal and "servants" at Balanced and Readable, as in 9:10.

decisions.choice: with Shimei
decisions.reason: Readable names Shimei for "him".

source.text: וְעָבְרָ֣ה הָעֲבָרָ֗ה לַֽעֲבִיר֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְשִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן־גֵּרָ֗א נָפַל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּעָבְר֖וֹ בַּיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And crossed the ford to bring over the household of the king, and to do the good in his eyes. And Shimei son of Gera fell before the king when he was crossing the Jordan.

en.L: And they kept crossing the ford to bring over the household of the king, and to do what [was] good in his eyes. And Shimei son of Gera fell down before the king as he was crossing the Jordan.
en.B: They kept crossing back and forth at the ford to bring the king's household over and to do whatever he wished. As the king was about to cross the Jordan, Shimei son of Gera fell down before him.
en.R: They went back and forth through the river at the crossing place, to bring the king's family over and to do whatever he wanted. As the king was crossing the Jordan, Shimei son of Gera bowed down to the ground in front of him.

es.L: Y cruzaban el vado para pasar a la casa del rey, y para hacer lo que [fuera] bueno a sus ojos. Y Simei hijo de Gera se postró delante del rey cuando él pasaba el Jordán.
es.B: Cruzaban el vado de un lado a otro para pasar a la familia del rey y para hacer todo lo que él quisiera. Cuando el rey iba a cruzar el Jordán, Simei hijo de Gera se postró delante de él.
es.R: Cruzaban el río de un lado a otro por el vado, para pasar a la familia del rey y para hacer todo lo que él quisiera. Mientras el rey cruzaba el Jordán, Simei hijo de Gera se inclinó hasta el suelo delante de él.

fr.L: Et ils passaient et repassaient le gué pour faire passer la maison du roi et pour faire ce qui [était] bon à ses yeux. Et Shiméï, fils de Guéra, tomba devant le roi au moment où il passait le Jourdain.
fr.B: Ils firent plusieurs fois l’aller et retour au gué pour faire passer la maison du roi et pour faire tout ce qu’il voudrait. Au moment où le roi allait passer le Jourdain, Shiméï, fils de Guéra, se jeta à ses pieds.
fr.R: Ils ont traversé plusieurs fois le fleuve à l’endroit du passage, pour faire passer la famille du roi et pour faire tout ce qu’il voulait. Pendant que le roi traversait le Jourdain, Shiméï, fils de Guéra, s’est jeté à terre devant lui.

vi.L: Họ cứ qua lại chỗ cạn để đưa gia đình vua sang, và để làm điều tốt trong mắt vua. Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra sấp mình xuống trước mặt vua khi vua qua sông Giô-đanh.
vi.B: Họ qua lại nhiều lần ở chỗ cạn để đưa hoàng gia sang sông và làm mọi điều vua muốn. Khi vua sắp qua sông Giô-đanh, Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra sấp mình xuống trước mặt vua.
vi.R: Họ đi tới đi lui qua chỗ cạn của sông để đưa gia đình vua sang, và làm mọi điều vua muốn. Khi vua đang qua sông Giô-đanh, Si-mê-i con trai Ghê-ra cúi sấp xuống đất trước mặt vua.

decisions.choice: they kept crossing the ford: repeated crossings to bring the household over
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads literally "and the ford crossed", which is hard to make sense of. The noun means a ford or crossing place (15:28; 17:16). This translation takes the clause as the men crossing again and again at the ford, as the verb form can describe a repeated action. Others read the noun as a ferry boat that kept crossing, or change one letter to read "they crossed the ford".

decisions.choice: do the good in his eyes: do whatever he wanted
decisions.reason: What is good in someone's eyes is what pleases them. The men of Benjamin and Ziba's household serve the king in any way he wishes.

decisions.choice: fell before the king: threw himself to the ground
decisions.reason: Lying face down before a king was the deepest sign of submission. The man who had cursed David now begs for his life.

decisions.choice: as he was crossing: at the moment of the crossing
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean as the king was about to cross or while he was crossing. Shimei meets him at the river.

decisions.choice: they kept crossing (Literal); back and forth (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The words follow meaning decision m1. Literal supplies "they" without brackets, since it reads the noun as the place, not the subject.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אַל־יַחֲשָׁב־לִ֣י אֲדֹנִי֮ עָוֺן֒ וְאַל־תִּזְכֹּ֗ר אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱוָ֣ה עַבְדְּךָ֔ בַּיּ֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יָׄצָ֥ׄאׄאֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לָשׂ֥וּם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־לִבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to the king, let not reckon to me my lord guilt, and do not remember what did wrong your servant on the day that my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, to set [it] the king to his heart.

en.L: And he said to the king, "Let my lord not count guilt against me, and do not remember what your servant did wrong on the day that my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, [nor] let the king take [it] to his heart.
en.B: He said to the king, "May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember the wrong your servant did on the day my lord the king went out from Jerusalem. Let the king put it out of his mind.
en.R: He said to the king, "Your Majesty, please do not hold my sin against me. Forget the wrong things I did on the day you left Jerusalem. Please do not keep thinking about them.

es.L: Y dijo al rey: «No me tome en cuenta mi señor la culpa, ni te acuerdes de lo que hizo mal tu siervo el día en que mi señor el rey salió de Jerusalén, [ni] lo ponga el rey en su corazón.
es.B: Le dijo al rey: «Que mi señor no me tenga por culpable. No te acuerdes del mal que hizo tu siervo el día en que mi señor el rey salió de Jerusalén. Que el rey lo borre de su mente.
es.R: Le dijo al rey: «Mi rey, por favor no me tomes en cuenta mi pecado. Olvida lo malo que hice el día en que saliste de Jerusalén. Por favor, no sigas pensando en eso.

fr.L: Et il dit au roi : « Que mon seigneur ne m’impute pas de faute, et ne te souviens pas de ce que ton serviteur a fait de mal le jour où mon seigneur le roi est sorti de Jérusalem, [et] que le roi ne [le] prenne pas à cœur.
fr.B: Il dit au roi : « Que mon seigneur ne me tienne pas pour coupable. Ne te souviens pas du mal que ton serviteur a fait le jour où mon seigneur le roi est sorti de Jérusalem. Que le roi l’oublie.
fr.R: Il a dit au roi : « Mon roi, s’il te plaît, ne me tiens pas rigueur de mon péché. Oublie le mal que j’ai fait le jour où tu as quitté Jérusalem. S’il te plaît, n’y pense plus.

vi.L: Ông nói với vua: "Xin chúa tôi đừng kể tội cho tôi, và đừng nhớ điều đầy tớ của vua đã làm sai trong ngày chúa tôi là vua ra khỏi Giê-ru-sa-lem; xin vua đừng để điều ấy vào lòng.
vi.B: Ông thưa với vua: "Xin bệ hạ đừng bắt tội tôi. Xin đừng nhớ đến điều sai trái đầy tớ của vua đã làm trong ngày bệ hạ rời Giê-ru-sa-lem. Xin bệ hạ bỏ qua cho.
vi.R: Ông thưa với vua: "Thưa đức vua, xin đừng bắt tội tôi. Xin quên đi những điều sai trái tôi đã làm trong ngày đức vua rời Giê-ru-sa-lem. Xin đức vua đừng nghĩ mãi đến chuyện ấy nữa.

decisions.choice: count guilt against me: hold me guilty and punish me
decisions.reason: The word for guilt covers both the wrong done and the punishment it deserves. To "count" it against someone is to keep it on their account (Psalm 32:2).

decisions.choice: what your servant did wrong on that day: the cursing at Bahurim
decisions.reason: Shimei had followed David along the hillside, cursing him and throwing stones and dirt (16:5-13).

decisions.choice: take it to his heart: keep thinking about it
decisions.reason: To set something on the heart is to take it seriously and dwell on it. Shimei asks that the king not let it weigh on him. The "not" of the first request carries over to this last clause.

decisions.choice: my lord ... your servant: speech of a subject to the king
decisions.reason: Shimei speaks of himself as "your servant" and of David as "my lord the king", the humble form of address to a king (9:11; 14:22).

decisions.choice: me, I; Your Majesty
decisions.reason: Readable turns the third-person courtesy into plain first and second person, and keeps the respect with "Your Majesty". Literal and Balanced keep "your servant".

source.text: כִּ֚י יָדַ֣ע עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י חָטָ֑אתִי וְהִנֵּֽה־בָ֣אתִי הַיּ֗וֹם רִאשׁוֹן֙ לְכָל־בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף לָרֶ֕דֶת לִקְרַ֖את אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For knows your servant that I have sinned; and look, I have come today, first of all [the] house of Joseph, to come down to meet my lord the king.

en.L: For your servant knows that I have sinned. And look, I have come today, first of all the house of Joseph, to come down to meet my lord the king."
en.B: Your servant knows that I have sinned. But see, today I have come, the first of all the house of Joseph, to come down and meet my lord the king."
en.R: I know that I have sinned. But look, today I am the first one from all the northern tribes to come down and meet you, my king."

es.L: Porque tu siervo sabe que he pecado. Y he aquí, he venido hoy, el primero de toda la casa de José, para bajar al encuentro de mi señor el rey».
es.B: Tu siervo sabe que ha pecado. Pero mira, hoy he venido, el primero de toda la casa de José, a bajar al encuentro de mi señor el rey».
es.R: Yo sé que he pecado. Pero mira, hoy soy el primero de todas las tribus del norte que ha bajado a recibirte, mi rey».

fr.L: Car ton serviteur sait que j’ai péché. Et voici, je suis venu aujourd’hui, le premier de toute la maison de Joseph, pour descendre à la rencontre de mon seigneur le roi. »
fr.B: Ton serviteur le sait, j’ai péché. Mais vois, je suis venu aujourd’hui, le premier de toute la maison de Joseph, pour descendre à la rencontre de mon seigneur le roi. »
fr.R: Je sais que j’ai péché. Mais regarde, aujourd’hui, je suis le premier de toutes les tribus du nord à descendre pour t’accueillir, mon roi. »

vi.L: Vì đầy tớ của vua biết rằng tôi đã phạm tội. Kìa, hôm nay tôi đã đến, là người đầu tiên của cả nhà Giô-sép, đi xuống đón chúa tôi là vua."
vi.B: Đầy tớ của vua biết rằng mình đã phạm tội. Nhưng hôm nay, tôi là người đầu tiên của cả nhà Giô-sép đã đến đây đón bệ hạ."
vi.R: Tôi biết mình đã phạm tội. Nhưng hôm nay tôi là người đầu tiên trong tất cả các chi tộc miền bắc xuống đây đón đức vua."

decisions.choice: the house of Joseph: the northern tribes
decisions.reason: Joseph was the father of Ephraim and Manasseh, the largest northern tribes, and his name could stand for the north as a whole (Joshua 18:5; 1 Kings 11:28). Shimei is from Benjamin, which lay between north and south, but he counts himself with the tribes outside Judah.

decisions.choice: your servant knows that I have sinned: an open confession
decisions.reason: Shimei admits his guilt outright and points to his early coming as proof of his change of heart.

decisions.choice: the northern tribes
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the house of Joseph" as the tribes it stands for.

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, Readable says "I" for "your servant".

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־צְרוּיָה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הֲתַ֣חַת זֹ֔את לֹ֥א יוּמַ֖ת שִׁמְעִ֑י כִּ֥י קִלֵּ֖ל אֶת־מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And answered Abishai son of Zeruiah and said, for this will not be put to death Shimei, for he cursed [the] anointed of Yahweh?

en.L: And Abishai son of Zeruiah answered and said, "Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed?"
en.B: Abishai son of Zeruiah spoke up and said, "Should not Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed!"
en.R: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shimei should be put to death for this! He cursed the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed."

es.L: Y Abisai hijo de Sarvia respondió y dijo: «¿No ha de morir Simei por esto, porque maldijo al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?».
es.B: Abisai hijo de Sarvia intervino y dijo: «¿No debería morir Simei por esto? ¡Maldijo al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!».
es.R: Entonces Abisai hijo de Sarvia dijo: «¡Simei debe morir por esto! Maldijo al rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido».

fr.L: Et Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, répondit et dit : « Shiméï ne sera-t-il pas mis à mort pour cela, parce qu’il a maudit l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? »
fr.B: Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, prit la parole : « Ne faut-il pas mettre à mort Shiméï pour cela ? Il a maudit l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! »
fr.R: Alors Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, a dit : « Shiméï doit être mis à mort pour cela ! Il a maudit le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint. »
