vi.L: A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia đáp lời và nói: "Vì việc này, chẳng lẽ Si-mê-i không bị xử tử sao, vì nó đã nguyền rủa người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?"
vi.B: A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia lên tiếng: "Chẳng lẽ Si-mê-i không phải chết vì việc này sao? Nó đã nguyền rủa người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!"
vi.R: Bấy giờ A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia nói: "Si-mê-i phải bị xử tử vì việc này! Nó đã nguyền rủa vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu."

decisions.choice: Abishai: Joab's brother, who wanted to kill Shimei before
decisions.reason: When Shimei cursed David, Abishai asked leave to go over and cut off his head, and David refused (16:9-11).

decisions.choice: he cursed the LORD's anointed: an offense against the king Yahweh chose
decisions.reason: The king was anointed at Yahweh's command, and the law forbade cursing a ruler of the people (Exodus 22:27). David himself had refused to harm Saul because he was Yahweh's anointed (1 Samuel 24:7; 26:9).

decisions.choice: shall not Shimei be put to death: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: Abishai is not asking for information but demanding the death penalty.

decisions.choice: the king the LORD has anointed; a statement
decisions.reason: As at 1 Samuel 24:7, Readable says what "anointed" means. It also turns the question into the statement it implies.

decisions.choice: "l’oint du SEIGNEUR" (L, B); "le roi que le SEIGNEUR a oint" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: Literal and Balanced keep "l’oint", Readable says who is meant. For the whole block.

decisions.choice: el ungido del SEÑOR (L, B); el rey que el SEÑOR ha ungido (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note, with the divine_name span on 'del SEÑOR' and 'el SEÑOR'.

decisions.choice: "người được xức dầu của CHÚA" (L, B); "vị vua CHÚA đã xức dầu" (R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note sets "vị vua được CHÚA xức dầu" for Balanced; here Balanced follows the English Balanced, which keeps "the LORD's anointed", and Readable takes the note's Readable form.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד מַה־לִּ֤י וְלָכֶם֙ בְּנֵ֣י צְרוּיָ֔ה כִּי־תִֽהְיוּ־לִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם לְשָׂטָ֑ן הַיּ֗וֹם י֤וּמַת אִישׁ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֚י הֲל֣וֹא יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם אֲנִי־מֶ֥לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, what to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah, that you become to me today an adversary? Today will be put to death a man in Israel? For do I not know that today I [am] king over Israel?

en.L: And David said, "What [is there] to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should become an adversary to me today? Shall anyone be put to death in Israel today? For do I not know that today I [am] king over Israel?"
en.B: David said, "Sons of Zeruiah, what business is this of yours? Why should you set yourselves against me today? Is anyone in Israel to be put to death on this day? Do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"
en.R: But David said, "You sons of Zeruiah, this is not your business! Today you are working against me. No one in Israel will be put to death today. I know that today I am king over Israel again."

es.L: Y David dijo: «¿Qué [hay] entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y yo, hijos de Sarvia, para que hoy me {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} adversarios? ¿Ha de morir hoy alguien en Israel? ¿Acaso no sé que hoy [soy] rey sobre Israel?».
es.B: David dijo: «Hijos de Sarvia, ¿qué tienen que ver {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con esto? ¿Por qué se {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} hoy en mi contra? ¿Ha de morir alguien en Israel en este día? ¿Acaso no sé que hoy soy rey sobre Israel?».
es.R: Pero David dijo: «Hijos de Sarvia, ¡esto no es asunto {{plural_you:suyo|vuestro}}! Hoy {{plural_you:están|estáis}} actuando en mi contra. Hoy nadie en Israel va a morir. Sé que hoy soy otra vez rey sobre Israel».

fr.L: Et David dit : « Qu’[y a-t-il] entre moi et vous, fils de Tserouya, pour que vous deveniez aujourd’hui pour moi un adversaire ? Aujourd’hui, quelqu’un serait-il mis à mort en Israël ? Ne sais-je donc pas qu’aujourd’hui je [suis] roi sur Israël ? »
fr.B: David répondit : « Fils de Tserouya, en quoi cela vous regarde-t-il ? Pourquoi vous dresser aujourd’hui contre moi ? Quelqu’un doit-il être mis à mort en Israël en un jour pareil ? Ne sais-je pas qu’aujourd’hui je suis roi sur Israël ? »
fr.R: Mais David a dit : « Fils de Tserouya, ce n’est pas votre affaire ! Aujourd’hui, vous agissez contre moi. Personne ne sera mis à mort en Israël aujourd’hui. Je sais qu’aujourd’hui, je suis de nouveau roi sur Israël. »

vi.L: Đa-vít nói: "Ta với các ngươi có [liên quan] gì, hỡi các con trai Xê-ru-gia, mà hôm nay các ngươi trở thành kẻ chống đối ta? Hôm nay có ai trong Y-sơ-ra-ên lại bị xử tử sao? Vì chẳng lẽ ta không biết rằng hôm nay ta [là] vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên sao?"
vi.B: Đa-vít nói: "Hỡi các con trai Xê-ru-gia, việc này có liên quan gì đến các ngươi? Sao hôm nay các ngươi lại chống đối ta? Ngày hôm nay mà lại có người trong Y-sơ-ra-ên bị xử tử sao? Chẳng lẽ ta không biết hôm nay ta là vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên sao?"
vi.R: Nhưng Đa-vít nói: "Hỡi các con trai Xê-ru-gia, việc này không liên quan đến các ngươi! Hôm nay các ngươi đang chống lại ta. Hôm nay sẽ không có ai trong Y-sơ-ra-ên bị xử tử. Ta biết rằng hôm nay ta lại làm vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên."

decisions.choice: what is there to me and to you: this is not your affair
decisions.reason: The phrase sets a distance between speaker and hearer and refuses what they propose. David used the same words to Abishai at Bahurim (16:10).

decisions.choice: adversary: one who opposes or stands in the way
decisions.reason: The word means an opponent or accuser, of a man as of a spiritual being (1 Samuel 29:4; 1 Kings 5:18). Here it is the sons of Zeruiah who would set themselves against the king's wish.

decisions.choice: today I am king over Israel: a day of restoring, not of revenge
decisions.reason: The day David regains his throne is to be marked by mercy, as Saul spared his opponents on the day of victory (1 Samuel 11:13). Executing a man of Saul's tribe could also have hardened the northern tribes against David.

decisions.choice: again; questions as statements
decisions.reason: Readable turns the rhetorical questions into the statements they imply and adds "again", since David is king once more after the revolt.

decisions.choice: Sons of Zeruiah first
decisions.reason: Balanced names the brothers first, as English often puts the person addressed at the start.

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Shimei, you will not die; and swore to him the king.

en.L: And the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king swore to him.
en.B: So the king said to Shimei, "You will not die." And the king gave him his oath.
en.R: Then the king told Shimei, "You will not be put to death." And the king made a promise to him with an oath.

es.L: Y el rey dijo a Simei: «No morirás». Y el rey se lo juró.
es.B: Así que el rey le dijo a Simei: «No morirás». Y el rey se lo juró.
es.R: Entonces el rey le dijo a Simei: «No te van a matar». Y el rey se lo prometió con un juramento.

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Shiméï : « Tu ne mourras pas. » Et le roi le lui jura.
fr.B: Le roi dit donc à Shiméï : « Tu ne mourras pas. » Et le roi le lui promit par serment.
fr.R: Ensuite, le roi a dit à Shiméï : « Tu ne seras pas mis à mort. » Et le roi le lui a promis par un serment.

vi.L: Vua nói với Si-mê-i: "Ngươi sẽ không chết." Và vua thề với ông.
vi.B: Vậy vua nói với Si-mê-i: "Ngươi sẽ không phải chết." Rồi vua thề với ông.
vi.R: Rồi vua bảo Si-mê-i: "Ngươi sẽ không bị xử tử." Và vua thề hứa với ông như vậy.

decisions.choice: swore to him: a binding promise of safety
decisions.reason: An oath in God's name bound the one who made it. David keeps his word, though before he dies he warns Solomon about Shimei, and Solomon later has him put to death for breaking his own oath (1 Kings 2:8-9, 36-46).

decisions.choice: be put to death
decisions.reason: Readable says "put to death" so that the promise is clearly about punishment, not about dying in general.

source.text: וּמְפִבֹ֨שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־שָׁא֔וּל יָרַ֖ד לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹא־עָשָׂ֨ה רַגְלָ֜יו וְלֹא־עָשָׂ֣ה שְׂפָמ֗וֹ וְאֶת־בְּגָדָיו֙ לֹ֣א כִבֵּ֔ס לְמִן־הַיּוֹם֙ לֶ֣כֶת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד־הַיּ֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥א בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Mephibosheth son of Saul came down to meet the king; and he had not done his feet, and had not done his mustache, and his clothes he had not washed, from the day the king went until the day that he came in peace.

en.L: And Mephibosheth son of Saul came down to meet the king. And he had not cared for his feet, and had not trimmed his mustache, and his clothes he had not washed, from the day the king went away until the day that he came [back] in peace.
en.B: Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, also came down to meet the king. From the day the king left until the day he returned safely, he had not tended his feet, trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes.
en.R: Saul's grandson Mephibosheth also came down to meet the king. From the day the king left until the day he came back safely, Mephibosheth had not taken care of his feet, trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes.

es.L: Y Mefiboset hijo de Saúl descendió al encuentro del rey. Y no había cuidado sus pies, ni se había arreglado el bigote, ni había lavado sus vestidos, desde el día en que el rey se fue hasta el día en que volvió en paz.
es.B: Mefiboset, el nieto de Saúl, también bajó a recibir al rey. Desde el día en que el rey se fue hasta el día en que volvió sano y salvo, no se había cuidado los pies, ni se había arreglado el bigote, ni había lavado su ropa.
es.R: Mefiboset, el nieto de Saúl, también bajó a recibir al rey. Desde el día en que el rey se fue hasta el día en que volvió sano y salvo, Mefiboset no se había cuidado los pies, ni se había recortado el bigote, ni había lavado su ropa.

fr.L: Et Mephibosheth, fils de Saül, descendit à la rencontre du roi. Et il n’avait pas soigné ses pieds, ni taillé sa moustache, et ses vêtements, il ne les avait pas lavés, depuis le jour où le roi était parti jusqu’au jour où il revint en paix.
fr.B: Mephibosheth, le petit-fils de Saül, descendit lui aussi à la rencontre du roi. Depuis le jour où le roi était parti jusqu’au jour de son retour en paix, il ne s’était pas soigné les pieds, ne s’était pas taillé la moustache et n’avait pas lavé ses vêtements.
fr.R: Mephibosheth, le petit-fils de Saül, est aussi descendu pour accueillir le roi. Depuis le jour où le roi était parti jusqu’au jour où il est revenu sain et sauf, Mephibosheth ne s’était pas soigné les pieds, ne s’était pas taillé la moustache et n’avait pas lavé ses vêtements.

vi.L: Mê-phi-bô-sết con trai Sau-lơ đi xuống đón vua. Ông đã không chăm sóc chân, không tỉa ria mép, không giặt áo quần, từ ngày vua ra đi cho đến ngày vua bình an [trở] về.
vi.B: Mê-phi-bô-sết, cháu nội Sau-lơ, cũng đi xuống đón vua. Từ ngày vua ra đi cho đến ngày vua bình an trở về, ông đã không chăm sóc chân, không tỉa ria mép, cũng không giặt áo quần.
vi.R: Mê-phi-bô-sết, cháu nội của Sau-lơ, cũng đi xuống đón vua. Từ ngày vua ra đi cho đến ngày vua bình an trở về, Mê-phi-bô-sết không chăm sóc chân, không tỉa ria mép và không giặt quần áo.

decisions.choice: feet, mustache and clothes left uncared for: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: A mourner let himself go: he covered or neglected his lip and beard, and wore unwashed clothes (Leviticus 13:45; Ezekiel 24:17). Mephibosheth had grieved for the whole of the king's exile, which speaks against Ziba's charge that he hoped to gain from it (16:3).

decisions.choice: had not done his feet: had not washed or tended them
decisions.reason: The verb "do" is used for grooming, as of trimming nails (Deuteronomy 21:12). Here it most likely means washing and caring for the feet, which needed daily care on dusty roads.

decisions.choice: son of Saul: Saul's grandson
decisions.reason: "Son" can mean any descendant. Mephibosheth was Jonathan's son and Saul's grandson (9:6).

decisions.choice: Saul's grandson
decisions.reason: As in chapter 9, Balanced and Readable say "grandson". They also add "also", since others have just come to meet the king.

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י כִּי־בָ֥א יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֛מָּה לֹא־הָלַ֥כְתָּ עִמִּ֖י מְפִיבֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when he came [from] Jerusalem to meet the king, that said to him the king, why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?

en.L: And it was, when he came [from] Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
en.B: When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
en.R: When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Mephibosheth, why did you not come with me when I left?"

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando vino [de] Jerusalén al encuentro del rey, el rey le dijo: «¿Por qué no fuiste conmigo, Mefiboset?».
es.B: Cuando llegó de Jerusalén a recibir al rey, el rey le preguntó: «¿Por qué no te fuiste conmigo, Mefiboset?».
es.R: Cuando llegó de Jerusalén a recibir al rey, el rey le preguntó: «Mefiboset, ¿por qué no te fuiste conmigo cuando me marché?».

fr.L: Et lorsqu’il vint [de] Jérusalem à la rencontre du roi, le roi lui dit : « Pourquoi n’es-tu pas venu avec moi, Mephibosheth ? »
fr.B: Quand il arriva de Jérusalem pour rencontrer le roi, le roi lui demanda : « Pourquoi n’es-tu pas parti avec moi, Mephibosheth ? »
fr.R: Quand il est arrivé de Jérusalem pour rencontrer le roi, le roi lui a demandé : « Mephibosheth, pourquoi n’es-tu pas venu avec moi quand je suis parti ? »

vi.L: Khi ông [từ] Giê-ru-sa-lem đến đón vua, vua nói với ông: "Sao ngươi không đi với ta, Mê-phi-bô-sết?"
vi.B: Khi ông từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến đón vua, vua hỏi: "Mê-phi-bô-sết, sao ngươi không đi với ta?"
vi.R: Khi ông từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến đón vua, vua hỏi: "Mê-phi-bô-sết, sao lúc ta ra đi ngươi không đi với ta?"

decisions.choice: he came from Jerusalem: Mephibosheth set out from the city
alternatives: when Jerusalem came to meet the king
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he came Jerusalem". This translation reads it with verse 25, where Mephibosheth "came down" to meet the king: he came from Jerusalem, where he lived (9:13). It could also mean "when he came to Jerusalem", the meeting taking place once the king had arrived, or "when Jerusalem came", that is, its people.

decisions.choice: why did you not go with me: the charge Ziba had made
decisions.reason: When David fled, Ziba told him that Mephibosheth had stayed in Jerusalem hoping to receive his grandfather's kingdom (16:3). The king's question gives Mephibosheth his chance to answer.

decisions.choice: when I left
decisions.reason: Readable adds when the king means, so the reader connects the question to the flight from Jerusalem.

source.text: וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַבְדִּ֣י רִמָּ֑נִי כִּֽי־אָמַ֨ר עַבְדְּךָ֜ אֶחְבְּשָׁה־לִּי֩ הַחֲמ֨וֹר וְאֶרְכַּ֤ב עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ וְאֵלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י פִסֵּ֖חַ עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, my lord the king, my servant deceived me; for said your servant, I will saddle for myself the donkey and I will ride on it and go with the king, for lame [is] your servant.

en.L: And he said, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, 'I will saddle the donkey for myself, and I will ride on it and go with the king,' for your servant [is] lame.
en.B: He answered, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me. Your servant said, 'I will have the donkey saddled for myself so that I can ride it and go with the king,' since your servant is lame.
en.R: He answered, "Your Majesty, my servant Ziba tricked me. I am lame, so I said, 'I will have my donkey saddled. Then I can ride on it and go with the king.'

es.L: Y él dijo: «Mi señor el rey, mi siervo me engañó. Porque tu siervo dijo: “Me aparejaré el asno, y montaré en él e iré con el rey”, porque tu siervo [es] cojo.
es.B: Él respondió: «Mi señor el rey, mi siervo me engañó. Tu siervo dijo: “Haré que me aparejen el asno para montarlo e ir con el rey”, porque tu siervo es cojo.
es.R: Él respondió: «Mi rey, mi siervo Siba me engañó. Como soy cojo, le dije: “Hazme aparejar el asno. Así podré montarlo e ir con el rey”.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Mon seigneur le roi, mon serviteur m’a trompé. Car ton serviteur avait dit : “Je me ferai seller l’âne, je le monterai et j’irai avec le roi”, car ton serviteur [est] boiteux.
fr.B: Il répondit : « Mon seigneur le roi, mon serviteur m’a trompé. Ton serviteur avait dit : “Je vais me faire seller l’âne, pour le monter et partir avec le roi”, car ton serviteur est boiteux.
fr.R: Il a répondu : « Mon seigneur le roi, mon serviteur Tsiba m’a trompé. Je suis boiteux, alors j’avais dit : “Je vais faire seller mon âne. Ensuite, je pourrai le monter et partir avec le roi.”

vi.L: Ông nói: "Thưa chúa tôi là vua, đầy tớ của tôi đã lừa tôi. Vì đầy tớ của vua đã nói: 'Tôi sẽ thắng yên lừa cho mình, cưỡi nó và đi với vua,' vì đầy tớ của vua [bị] què.
vi.B: Ông thưa: "Tâu bệ hạ, đầy tớ của tôi đã lừa tôi. Đầy tớ của vua đã bảo: 'Hãy thắng yên lừa cho tôi để tôi cưỡi đi theo vua,' vì đầy tớ của vua bị què.
vi.R: Ông thưa: "Thưa đức vua, Xíp-ba đầy tớ của tôi đã lừa tôi. Tôi bị què, nên tôi đã bảo: 'Hãy thắng yên lừa cho tôi. Rồi tôi sẽ cưỡi nó đi theo vua.'

decisions.choice: deceived me: betrayed my trust
decisions.reason: The verb means to trick or betray. Mephibosheth says that Ziba left without him, taking the donkeys and supplies to David himself (16:1-2), and then lied about him.

decisions.choice: I will saddle for myself: Mephibosheth's own plan, following the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "I will saddle for myself". The ancient Greek and Syriac translations read "saddle for me", an order given to Ziba. Either way, Mephibosheth meant to go and needed Ziba's help to do it.

decisions.choice: lame: unable to walk
decisions.reason: Mephibosheth had been lame in both feet since a fall when he was five (4:4; 9:13). He could not follow the king on foot.

decisions.choice: I will have the donkey saddled
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "have ... saddled", since a lame man would need others to saddle it, without changing who made the plan. Literal keeps "I will saddle".

decisions.choice: my servant Ziba; I
decisions.reason: Readable names Ziba, says "I" for "your servant" and "Your Majesty" for "my lord the king", and puts the lameness first as the reason for the plan.

source.text: וַיְרַגֵּ֣ל בְּעַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he slandered your servant to my lord the king; and my lord the king [is] like the angel of God; and do the good in your eyes.

en.L: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king [is] like an angel of God; so do what [is] good in your eyes.
en.B: He has told my lord the king lies about your servant. Yet my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do whatever seems good to you.
en.R: He has told you lies about me. But Your Majesty is like an angel from God, who knows what is right. So do whatever you think is best.

es.L: Y él ha calumniado a tu siervo ante mi señor el rey. Pero mi señor el rey [es] como un ángel de Dios; haz, pues, lo que [sea] bueno a tus ojos.
es.B: Él le ha contado mentiras a mi señor el rey acerca de tu siervo. Pero mi señor el rey es como un ángel de Dios; así que haz lo que te parezca bien.
es.R: Te ha contado mentiras sobre mí. Pero tú, mi rey, eres como un ángel enviado por Dios, que sabe lo que es justo. Así que haz lo que creas mejor.

fr.L: Et il a calomnié ton serviteur auprès de mon seigneur le roi. Mais mon seigneur le roi [est] comme un ange de Dieu ; fais donc ce qui [est] bon à tes yeux.
fr.B: Il a dit des mensonges sur ton serviteur à mon seigneur le roi. Mais mon seigneur le roi est comme un ange de Dieu : fais donc ce qui te semble bon.
fr.R: Il t’a raconté des mensonges sur moi. Mais toi, mon roi, tu es comme un ange venu de Dieu, qui sait ce qui est juste. Alors fais ce que tu penses être le mieux.

vi.L: Nó đã vu khống đầy tớ của vua với chúa tôi là vua. Nhưng chúa tôi là vua như thiên sứ của Đức Chúa Trời; vậy xin vua làm điều tốt trong mắt vua.
vi.B: Nó đã nói dối bệ hạ về đầy tớ của vua. Nhưng bệ hạ như một thiên sứ của Đức Chúa Trời, vậy xin bệ hạ làm điều gì bệ hạ thấy là tốt.
vi.R: Nó đã nói dối đức vua về tôi. Nhưng đức vua như một thiên sứ từ Đức Chúa Trời, biết điều gì là đúng. Vậy xin đức vua làm điều gì đức vua thấy là tốt nhất.

decisions.choice: slandered: spread false reports
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for foot and means to go about telling tales against someone (Psalm 15:3).

decisions.choice: like an angel of God: able to see the truth and judge rightly
decisions.reason: The woman of Tekoa used the same words of David's wisdom in telling good from bad (14:17, 20). Mephibosheth leaves the judgment to the king's discernment.

decisions.choice: do what is good in your eyes: do what you think best
decisions.reason: He puts himself fully in the king's hands, as in verse 19.

decisions.choice: an angel of God
decisions.reason: As in 14:17 and 14:20, Literal and Balanced say "an angel", since the comparison is to any messenger of God, not one in particular.

decisions.choice: who knows what is right
decisions.reason: Readable adds the point of the comparison from meaning decision m2, and says "me" for "your servant".

source.text: כִּי֩ לֹ֨א הָיָ֜ה כָּל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֗י כִּ֤י אִם־אַנְשֵׁי־מָ֨וֶת֙ לַאדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתָּ֨שֶׁת֙ אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֔ בְּאֹכְלֵ֖י שֻׁלְחָנֶ֑ךָ וּמַה־יֶּשׁ־לִ֥י עוֹד֙ צְדָקָ֔ה וְלִזְעֹ֥ק ע֖וֹד אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For was not all [the] house of my father but men of death to my lord the king, and you set your servant among those eating at your table; and what is there to me still [of] right, and to cry out still to the king?

en.L: For all the house of my father were nothing but men of death to my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. And what right do I still have, to cry out any more to the king?"
en.B: My father's whole house deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, yet you gave your servant a place among those who eat at your table. So what right do I have to make any more appeals to the king?"
en.R: All of my grandfather Saul's family deserved to be put to death by you, Your Majesty. But you let me eat at your own table. So I have no right to ask the king for anything more."

es.L: Porque toda la casa de mi padre no [era] sino hombres de muerte ante mi señor el rey, y tú pusiste a tu siervo entre los que comen a tu mesa. ¿Y qué derecho tengo aún, para clamar más al rey?».
es.B: Toda la casa de mi padre no merecía de mi señor el rey otra cosa que la muerte, y sin embargo diste a tu siervo un lugar entre los que comen a tu mesa. ¿Qué derecho tengo, pues, de seguir haciéndole peticiones al rey?».
es.R: Toda la familia de mi abuelo Saúl merecía que tú, mi rey, la condenaras a muerte. Pero tú me dejaste comer a tu propia mesa. Así que no tengo derecho a pedirle nada más al rey».

fr.L: Car toute la maison de mon père n’était que des hommes de mort pour mon seigneur le roi, et tu as placé ton serviteur parmi ceux qui mangent à ta table. Et quel droit ai-je encore, pour crier encore vers le roi ? »
fr.B: Toute la famille de mon père ne méritait que la mort de la part de mon seigneur le roi, et pourtant tu as donné à ton serviteur une place parmi ceux qui mangent à ta table. Quel droit aurais-je donc encore d’adresser des plaintes au roi ? »
fr.R: Toute la famille de mon grand-père Saül méritait que tu la fasses mourir, mon roi. Mais tu m’as permis de manger à ta propre table. Je n’ai donc aucun droit de demander encore quelque chose au roi. »

vi.L: Vì cả nhà cha tôi đều chỉ là những người đáng chết trước chúa tôi là vua, thế mà vua lại đặt đầy tớ của vua vào hàng những người ăn tại bàn vua. Vậy tôi còn quyền gì để kêu xin vua nữa?"
vi.B: Cả nhà ông nội tôi đáng bị bệ hạ xử tử, thế mà bệ hạ lại cho đầy tớ của vua được ngồi ăn chung bàn với bệ hạ. Vậy tôi còn quyền gì mà kêu xin bệ hạ nữa?"
vi.R: Cả gia đình của ông nội tôi là Sau-lơ đều đáng bị đức vua xử tử. Nhưng đức vua lại cho tôi được ăn tại bàn của đức vua. Vì vậy tôi không có quyền xin đức vua điều gì thêm nữa."

decisions.choice: men of death: men who deserved to die
decisions.reason: A "man of death" or "son of death" is one who is condemned or worthy of death (12:5; 1 Samuel 26:16). As members of the old royal house, Saul's family could have expected to be wiped out by the new king.

decisions.choice: among those who eat at your table: David's kindness in 9:7-13
decisions.reason: David had given Mephibosheth a place at the royal table for Jonathan's sake.

decisions.choice: right: a just claim
decisions.reason: The word often means righteousness; here it means a claim one can rightly make. Mephibosheth says he has no grounds for asking more.

decisions.choice: the house of my father: Saul's family
decisions.reason: "My father's house" means the family line he belongs to, the house of Saul.

decisions.choice: my grandfather Saul's family; a statement
decisions.reason: Readable names Saul so the reader does not think of Jonathan alone, and turns the closing question into the statement it implies.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֛מָּה תְּדַבֵּ֥ר ע֖וֹד דְּבָרֶ֑יךָ אָמַ֕רְתִּי אַתָּ֣ה וְצִיבָ֔א תַּחְלְק֖וּ אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him the king, why do you speak still your words? I have said, you and Ziba will divide the field.

en.L: And the king said to him, "Why do you still speak your words? I have said: you and Ziba shall divide the land."
en.B: The king said to him, "Why say any more about your affairs? I have decided: you and Ziba are to divide the land."
en.R: The king said to him, "You do not need to say any more. I have decided that you and Ziba will divide the land between you."

es.L: Y el rey le dijo: «¿Por qué sigues hablando de tus asuntos? Yo he dicho: Tú y Siba {{plural_you:se repartirán|os repartiréis}} las tierras».
es.B: El rey le dijo: «¿Para qué decir más sobre tus asuntos? Ya lo he decidido: tú y Siba {{plural_you:se repartirán|os repartiréis}} las tierras».
es.R: El rey le dijo: «No necesitas decir nada más. He decidido que tú y Siba {{plural_you:se repartan|os repartáis}} las tierras entre los dos».

fr.L: Et le roi lui dit : « Pourquoi dis-tu encore tes paroles ? Je l’ai dit : toi et Tsiba, vous partagerez le champ. »
fr.B: Le roi lui dit : « À quoi bon parler encore de tes affaires ? J’ai décidé : toi et Tsiba, vous partagerez les terres. »
fr.R: Le roi lui a dit : « Tu n’as pas besoin d’en dire plus. J’ai décidé que toi et Tsiba, vous partagerez les terres entre vous. »

vi.L: Vua nói với ông: "Sao ngươi còn nói những lời của ngươi? Ta đã nói: ngươi và Xíp-ba sẽ chia đất với nhau."
vi.B: Vua bảo ông: "Ngươi không cần nói thêm về chuyện của ngươi nữa. Ta đã quyết định: ngươi và Xíp-ba sẽ chia đất với nhau."
vi.R: Vua bảo ông: "Ngươi không cần nói thêm gì nữa. Ta đã quyết định ngươi và Xíp-ba sẽ chia nhau phần đất ấy."

decisions.choice: I have said: I have decided
decisions.reason: The verb "say" can mean to state a decision, especially in the mouth of a king.

decisions.choice: you and Ziba shall divide the land: a new ruling
decisions.reason: David first gave all Saul's land to Mephibosheth (9:7-10), then, on Ziba's word, all of it to Ziba (16:4). Now he divides it. The story does not say whether he did so because he could not tell who was telling the truth.

decisions.choice: the field: the family's land
decisions.reason: "Field" means the estate as a whole, as in 9:7.

decisions.choice: your affairs
decisions.reason: Balanced takes "your words" in its sense of "your matters", the case Mephibosheth is pleading.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מְפִיבֹ֨שֶׁת֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ גַּ֥ם אֶת־הַכֹּ֖ל יִקָּ֑ח אַ֠חֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֞א אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶךבְּשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Mephibosheth to the king, also the whole let him take, after that has come my lord the king in peace to his house.

en.L: And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take even the whole, since my lord the king has come in peace to his house."
en.B: Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all, now that my lord the king has come home safely."
en.R: Mephibosheth said to the king, "He can have all of it. It is enough for me that Your Majesty has come home safely."

es.L: Y Mefiboset dijo al rey: «Que tome aun todo, ya que mi señor el rey ha vuelto en paz a su casa».
es.B: Mefiboset le dijo al rey: «Que se quede con todo, ahora que mi señor el rey ha vuelto sano y salvo a su casa».
es.R: Mefiboset le dijo al rey: «Que se quede con todo. Me basta con que tú, mi rey, hayas vuelto a casa sano y salvo».

fr.L: Et Mephibosheth dit au roi : « Qu’il prenne même tout, puisque mon seigneur le roi est revenu en paix dans sa maison. »
fr.B: Mephibosheth dit au roi : « Qu’il prenne tout, maintenant que mon seigneur le roi est rentré chez lui sain et sauf. »
fr.R: Mephibosheth a dit au roi : « Il peut tout prendre. Pour moi, ce qui compte, c’est que toi, mon roi, tu sois rentré chez toi sain et sauf. »

vi.L: Mê-phi-bô-sết nói với vua: "Cứ để nó lấy cả, vì chúa tôi là vua đã bình an trở về cung mình."
vi.B: Mê-phi-bô-sết thưa với vua: "Cứ để nó lấy hết, miễn là bệ hạ đã bình an trở về cung."
vi.R: Mê-phi-bô-sết thưa với vua: "Nó lấy hết cũng được. Đối với tôi, đức vua bình an trở về là đủ rồi."

decisions.choice: since: now that
decisions.reason: The words mean "after", here giving the reason: the king's safe return is all Mephibosheth wanted.

decisions.choice: in peace: safe and well
decisions.reason: "Peace" here is safety and wholeness, as in verse 25.

decisions.choice: let him take it all: the story leaves the reader to judge
decisions.reason: The narrator does not say whether Ziba or Mephibosheth told the truth. Mephibosheth's unkempt state (verse 25) and his readiness to give up the land both count in his favor.

decisions.choice: It is enough for me
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain the reason implied by "since": the king's return matters more to him than the land.

source.text: וּבַרְזִלַּי֙ הַגִּלְעָדִ֔י יָרַ֖ד מֵרֹגְלִ֑ים וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר אֶת־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לְשַׁלְּח֖וֹ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim, and he crossed with the king the Jordan, to send him off [over] the Jordan.

en.L: And Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim, and he crossed the Jordan with the king, to send him off [over] the Jordan.
en.B: Barzillai the Gileadite had also come down from Rogelim, and he crossed the Jordan with the king to see him on his way across the river.
en.R: Barzillai from Gilead had also come down from his town of Rogelim. He crossed the Jordan River with the king, to go with him for the first part of his journey.

es.L: Y Barzilai el galaadita había descendido de Rogelim, y pasó el Jordán con el rey, para despedirlo [al otro lado] del Jordán.
es.B: Barzilai el galaadita también había bajado de Rogelim, y cruzó el Jordán con el rey para despedirlo al otro lado del río.
es.R: Barzilai, de Galaad, también había bajado de su pueblo de Rogelim. Cruzó el río Jordán con el rey, para acompañarlo en el primer tramo del viaje.

fr.L: Et Barzillaï le Galaadite était descendu de Roguelim, et il passa le Jourdain avec le roi, pour l’accompagner [au-delà] du Jourdain.
fr.B: Barzillaï le Galaadite était aussi descendu de Roguelim, et il passa le Jourdain avec le roi pour l’accompagner de l’autre côté du fleuve.
fr.R: Barzillaï, de Galaad, était aussi descendu de sa ville de Roguelim. Il a traversé le Jourdain avec le roi, pour faire avec lui le début de son voyage.

vi.L: Bát-xi-lai người Ga-la-át đã từ Rô-ghê-lim đi xuống, và ông qua sông Giô-đanh với vua để tiễn vua [qua] sông Giô-đanh.
vi.B: Bát-xi-lai người Ga-la-át cũng từ Rô-ghê-lim xuống, và ông qua sông Giô-đanh với vua để tiễn vua sang bên kia sông.
vi.R: Bát-xi-lai người Ga-la-át cũng từ quê ông là Rô-ghê-lim đi xuống. Ông qua sông Giô-đanh với vua, để đi cùng vua một đoạn đường đầu.

decisions.choice: Barzillai: one of those who fed David in exile
decisions.reason: When David reached Mahanaim, Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim brought beds, bowls and food for him and his people (17:27-29).

decisions.choice: the Gileadite from Rogelim: from Gilead, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead is the highland east of the Jordan where Mahanaim lay. Rogelim was a town there whose exact place is unknown.

decisions.choice: to send him off: to escort him for the first part of the way
decisions.reason: To "send off" a guest is to go with him for a short distance (Genesis 18:16). Verse 37 shows that Barzillai meant to go only a little way beyond the river.

decisions.choice: to go with him for the first part of his journey
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom of sending a guest off from meaning decision m3, and adds "his town of" before Rogelim.

source.text: וּבַרְזִלַּי֙ זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֔ד בֶּן־שְׁמֹנִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וְהֽוּא־כִלְכַּ֤ל אֶת־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בְּשִׁיבָת֣וֹ בְמַחֲנַ֔יִם כִּֽי־אִ֛ישׁ גָּד֥וֹל ה֖וּא מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And Barzillai [was] very old, a son of eighty years; and he had provided for the king during his stay at Mahanaim, for a very great man [was] he.

en.L: And Barzillai [was] very old, eighty years old. And he had provided for the king while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he [was] a very great man.
en.B: Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age. He had supplied the king's needs while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
en.R: Barzillai was a very old man. He was eighty years old. He had given the king food and supplies while he was staying at Mahanaim, because he was very rich.

es.L: Y Barzilai [era] muy anciano, de ochenta años. Y él había provisto al rey mientras estuvo en Mahanaim, porque [era] un hombre muy grande.
es.B: Barzilai era muy anciano; tenía ochenta años. Le había dado al rey lo que necesitaba mientras estuvo en Mahanaim, porque era un hombre muy rico.
es.R: Barzilai era un hombre muy anciano. Tenía ochenta años. Le había dado al rey comida y provisiones mientras estuvo en Mahanaim, porque era muy rico.

fr.L: Et Barzillaï [était] très vieux, âgé de quatre-vingts ans. Et il avait entretenu le roi pendant son séjour à Mahanaïm, car c’[était] un homme très considérable.
fr.B: Barzillaï était très âgé : il avait quatre-vingts ans. Il avait pourvu aux besoins du roi pendant son séjour à Mahanaïm, car c’était un homme très riche.
fr.R: Barzillaï était un homme très âgé. Il avait quatre-vingts ans. Il avait donné au roi de la nourriture et tout ce qu’il lui fallait pendant que le roi était à Mahanaïm, car il était très riche.

vi.L: Bát-xi-lai [đã] rất già, tám mươi tuổi. Ông đã cung cấp cho vua trong thời gian vua ở Ma-ha-na-im, vì ông [là] một người rất giàu có.
vi.B: Bát-xi-lai đã rất già, tám mươi tuổi. Ông đã cung cấp mọi nhu cầu cho vua trong thời gian vua ở Ma-ha-na-im, vì ông là người rất giàu có.
vi.R: Bát-xi-lai là một ông lão đã tám mươi tuổi. Ông đã cung cấp thức ăn và mọi thứ cần dùng cho vua trong thời gian vua ở Ma-ha-na-im, vì ông rất giàu.

decisions.choice: a son of eighty years: eighty years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as "son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: provided for: supplied food and all he needed
decisions.reason: The verb means to sustain or provide with food (Genesis 45:11; 50:21). The king uses the same verb in his offer in verse 34.

decisions.choice: a very great man: a man of great wealth and standing
decisions.reason: "Great" describes a man's wealth and importance, as of Nabal (1 Samuel 25:2).

decisions.choice: wealthy (Balanced); rich (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the kind of greatness the context points to: he had the means to feed the king's company.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־בַּרְזִלָּ֑י אַתָּה֙ עֲבֹ֣ר אִתִּ֔י וְכִלְכַּלְתִּ֥י אֹתְךָ֛ עִמָּדִ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Barzillai, you, cross over with me, and I will provide for you with me in Jerusalem.

en.L: And the king said to Barzillai, "You, cross over with me, and I will provide for you with me in Jerusalem."
en.B: The king said to Barzillai, "Come across with me, and I will provide for you in Jerusalem, at my side."
en.R: The king said to Barzillai, "Come across the river with me. Live with me in Jerusalem, and I will take care of you."

es.L: Y el rey dijo a Barzilai: «Tú, pasa conmigo, y yo te sustentaré conmigo en Jerusalén».
es.B: El rey le dijo a Barzilai: «Cruza conmigo, y yo te sustentaré en Jerusalén, a mi lado».
es.R: El rey le dijo a Barzilai: «Cruza el río conmigo. Ven a vivir conmigo en Jerusalén, y yo te cuidaré».

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Barzillaï : « Toi, passe avec moi, et je t’entretiendrai auprès de moi à Jérusalem. »
fr.B: Le roi dit à Barzillaï : « Passe le fleuve avec moi, et je pourvoirai à tes besoins à Jérusalem, auprès de moi. »
fr.R: Le roi a dit à Barzillaï : « Traverse le fleuve avec moi. Viens vivre avec moi à Jérusalem, et je m’occuperai de toi. »

vi.L: Vua nói với Bát-xi-lai: "Ông hãy qua sông với ta, ta sẽ cung cấp cho ông ở với ta tại Giê-ru-sa-lem."
vi.B: Vua nói với Bát-xi-lai: "Ông hãy qua sông với ta, ta sẽ chu cấp cho ông ở bên ta tại Giê-ru-sa-lem."
vi.R: Vua nói với Bát-xi-lai: "Ông hãy qua sông với ta. Hãy đến sống với ta ở Giê-ru-sa-lem, ta sẽ chăm lo cho ông."

decisions.choice: I will provide for you: repaying kindness with kindness
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Barzillai in verse 33. As he provided for the king, the king will now provide for him.

decisions.choice: with me in Jerusalem: as a guest at the royal court
decisions.reason: To be provided for at the king's side meant living at court and eating at the king's table, an honor like Mephibosheth's (9:7; 1 Kings 2:7).

decisions.choice: the river; Live with me
decisions.reason: Readable says what is crossed and spells out that the offer is to live at court.

decisions.choice: the king says "ông" to Barzillai; Barzillai says "vua" / "bệ hạ" / "đức vua" and "đầy tớ của vua" / "tôi"
decisions.reason: Barzillai is an old and honoured man who fed the king; David speaks to him with respect, as to Zadok and Hushai.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר בַּרְזִלַּ֖י אֶל־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כַּמָּ֗ה יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיַּ֔י כִּי־אֶעֱלֶ֥ה אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Barzillai to the king, how many [are the] days of [the] years of my life, that I should go up with the king [to] Jerusalem?

en.L: And Barzillai said to the king, "How many [are] the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king [to] Jerusalem?
en.B: But Barzillai answered the king, "How many years do I have left to live, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
en.R: But Barzillai answered the king, "I do not have many years left to live. Why should I go up to Jerusalem with you, Your Majesty?

es.L: Y Barzilai dijo al rey: «¿Cuántos [son] los días de los años de mi vida, para que yo suba con el rey [a] Jerusalén?
es.B: Pero Barzilai le respondió al rey: «¿Cuántos años me quedan de vida, para que suba a Jerusalén con el rey?
es.R: Pero Barzilai le respondió al rey: «No me quedan muchos años de vida. ¿Para qué voy a subir contigo a Jerusalén, mi rey?

fr.L: Et Barzillaï dit au roi : « Combien [sont] les jours des années de ma vie, pour que je monte avec le roi [à] Jérusalem ?
fr.B: Mais Barzillaï répondit au roi : « Combien d’années me reste-t-il à vivre, pour que je monte à Jérusalem avec le roi ?
fr.R: Mais Barzillaï a répondu au roi : « Il ne me reste plus beaucoup d’années à vivre. Pourquoi monterais-je à Jérusalem avec toi, mon roi ?

vi.L: Bát-xi-lai nói với vua: "Những ngày trong những năm đời tôi [còn] bao nhiêu, mà tôi lại đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem với vua?
vi.B: Nhưng Bát-xi-lai thưa với vua: "Tôi còn sống được bao nhiêu năm nữa mà phải đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem với bệ hạ?
vi.R: Nhưng Bát-xi-lai thưa với vua: "Tôi không còn sống được bao nhiêu năm nữa. Thưa đức vua, sao tôi lại phải lên Giê-ru-sa-lem với đức vua?

decisions.choice: how many are the days of the years of my life: I have little time left
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "not many". Barzillai means that at his age a new life at court makes no sense (compare Genesis 47:8-9).

decisions.choice: go up: travel to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: One always goes "up" to Jerusalem, which stands high in the hill country, far above the Jordan valley.

decisions.choice: a statement and a question
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the first question implies, and keeps a simple "why" question for the rest.

source.text: בֶּן־שְׁמֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָה֩ אָנֹכִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם הַאֵדַ֣ע׀בֵּין־ט֣וֹב לְרָ֗ע אִם־יִטְעַ֤ם עַבְדְּךָ֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֹכַל֙ וְאֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶשְׁתֶּ֔ה אִם־אֶשְׁמַ֣ע ע֔וֹד בְּק֖וֹל שָׁרִ֣ים וְשָׁר֑וֹת וְלָמָּה֩ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ עוֹד֙ לְמַשָּׂ֔א אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of eighty years I [am] today; do I know between good and bad? Or will taste your servant what I eat and what I drink? Or will I hear still [the] voice of male singers and female singers? And why will be your servant still a burden to my lord the king?

en.L: I [am] eighty years old today. Can I know [the difference] between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I still hear the voice of men singers and women singers? And why should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king?
en.B: I am eighty years old today. Can I still tell what is pleasant from what is not? Can your servant taste what I eat and drink? Do I still hear the voices of men and women singing? Why should your servant be one more burden to my lord the king?
en.R: I am already eighty years old. I can no longer enjoy the good things of life. I cannot taste what I eat or drink. I cannot hear the voices of men and women when they sing. I would only be a burden to you, my king.

es.L: Ochenta años tengo hoy. ¿Puedo yo distinguir entre lo bueno y lo malo? ¿Puede tu siervo gustar lo que come o lo que bebe? ¿Puedo oír aún la voz de los cantores y de las cantoras? ¿Y por qué ha de ser tu siervo una carga más para mi señor el rey?
es.B: Hoy tengo ochenta años. ¿Puedo todavía distinguir lo agradable de lo que no lo es? ¿Puede tu siervo saborear lo que come y lo que bebe? ¿Oigo todavía la voz de los hombres y de las mujeres que cantan? ¿Por qué ha de ser tu siervo una carga más para mi señor el rey?
es.R: Ya tengo ochenta años. Ya no puedo disfrutar de las cosas buenas de la vida. No le siento el sabor a lo que como ni a lo que bebo. No puedo oír las voces de los hombres y las mujeres cuando cantan. Solo sería una carga para ti, mi rey.

fr.L: J’[ai] aujourd’hui quatre-vingts ans. Puis-je connaître [la différence] entre le bon et le mauvais ? Ton serviteur peut-il goûter ce que je mange et ce que je bois ? Puis-je entendre encore la voix des chanteurs et des chanteuses ? Et pourquoi ton serviteur serait-il encore à charge à mon seigneur le roi ?
fr.B: J’ai aujourd’hui quatre-vingts ans. Suis-je encore capable de distinguer ce qui est agréable de ce qui ne l’est pas ? Ton serviteur peut-il goûter ce qu’il mange et ce qu’il boit ? Puis-je encore entendre la voix des chanteurs et des chanteuses ? Pourquoi ton serviteur serait-il une charge de plus pour mon seigneur le roi ?
fr.R: J’ai déjà quatre-vingts ans. Je ne peux plus profiter des bonnes choses de la vie. Je ne sens plus le goût de ce que je mange ou de ce que je bois. Je n’entends plus la voix des hommes et des femmes quand ils chantent. Je serais seulement une charge pour toi, mon roi.

vi.L: Hôm nay tôi [đã] tám mươi tuổi. Tôi có thể biết [phân biệt] giữa điều tốt và điều xấu không? Đầy tớ của vua có thể nếm được món tôi ăn hay món tôi uống không? Tôi còn có thể nghe tiếng của các ca sĩ nam và ca sĩ nữ không? Sao đầy tớ của vua lại còn làm gánh nặng cho chúa tôi là vua?
vi.B: Năm nay tôi đã tám mươi tuổi. Tôi còn phân biệt được điều gì thú vị điều gì không sao? Đầy tớ của vua còn nếm được mùi vị của món ăn thức uống sao? Tôi còn nghe được tiếng hát của nam nữ ca sĩ sao? Sao đầy tớ của vua lại còn làm gánh nặng cho bệ hạ nữa?
vi.R: Tôi đã tám mươi tuổi rồi. Tôi không còn hưởng được những điều thú vị trong đời nữa. Tôi không còn nếm được mùi vị của món ăn thức uống. Tôi cũng không còn nghe rõ tiếng nam nữ ca hát. Tôi chỉ làm gánh nặng cho đức vua mà thôi.

decisions.choice: know between good and bad: tell what is pleasant from what is not
decisions.reason: In this setting, next to tasting food and hearing music, the phrase most likely means the ability to enjoy, to tell a pleasant thing from an unpleasant one. It can also mean judging right from wrong, as in Deuteronomy 1:39, but Barzillai is speaking of the pleasures of court life.

decisions.choice: men singers and women singers: music at the royal court
decisions.reason: Kings kept singers to perform at feasts (Ecclesiastes 2:8; Amos 6:5). Life at court would offer pleasures Barzillai can no longer enjoy.

decisions.choice: burden: a load to be carried
decisions.reason: Barzillai means that the king would have to support an old man who could give nothing in return. David used the same word when he told Hushai that he would be a burden if he came with him (15:33).

decisions.choice: [the difference] (Literal); what is pleasant from what is not (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the word English needs after "between". Balanced puts the sense of meaning decision m1 into words.

decisions.choice: statements for questions; I and you for your servant and my lord
decisions.reason: Each question expects the answer "no", so Readable states the answers. It says "I" for "your servant".

source.text: כִּמְעַ֞ט יַעֲבֹ֧ר עַבְדְּךָ֛ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן אֶת־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלָ֨מָּה֙ יִגְמְלֵ֣נִי הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הַגְּמוּלָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: Like a little will cross your servant the Jordan with the king; and why will repay me the king this repayment?

en.L: Your servant will cross the Jordan with the king only a little way. And why should the king repay me with this reward?
en.B: Your servant will go only a short way across the Jordan with the king. Why should the king give me a reward like this?
en.R: I will just go a little way across the Jordan with you. You do not need to reward me like this.

es.L: Tu siervo pasará el Jordán con el rey solo un poco. ¿Y por qué ha de pagarme el rey con esta recompensa?
es.B: Tu siervo cruzará el Jordán con el rey solo un trecho corto. ¿Por qué ha de darme el rey una recompensa así?
es.R: Solo cruzaré contigo un poco más allá del Jordán. No hace falta que me recompenses así.

fr.L: Ton serviteur passera le Jourdain avec le roi juste un peu. Et pourquoi le roi me rendrait-il cette récompense ?
fr.B: Ton serviteur fera seulement un bout de chemin avec le roi au-delà du Jourdain. Pourquoi le roi me donnerait-il une telle récompense ?
fr.R: Je vais juste faire un petit bout de chemin avec toi de l’autre côté du Jourdain. Tu n’as pas besoin de me récompenser ainsi.

vi.L: Đầy tớ của vua sẽ chỉ qua sông Giô-đanh với vua một quãng ngắn thôi. Sao vua lại phải đền đáp tôi phần thưởng này?
vi.B: Đầy tớ của vua chỉ xin đi qua sông Giô-đanh với bệ hạ một quãng ngắn thôi. Sao bệ hạ lại ban cho tôi phần thưởng như thế?
vi.R: Tôi chỉ xin đi với đức vua qua sông Giô-đanh một đoạn ngắn thôi. Đức vua không cần phải thưởng cho tôi như vậy đâu.

decisions.choice: like a little: only a short distance
decisions.reason: Barzillai will escort the king across the river and a little beyond, as one sends off a guest (verse 32), and then return home.

decisions.choice: repay ... this reward: return his kindness
decisions.reason: The verb and noun mean to deal out what someone has earned, good or bad. Barzillai counts what he did as no great service, needing no such reward.

decisions.choice: You do not need to reward me like this
decisions.reason: Readable turns the polite question into the statement it implies.

source.text: יָֽשָׁב־נָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאָמֻ֣ת בְּעִירִ֔י עִ֛ם קֶ֥בֶר אָבִ֖י וְאִמִּ֑י וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀עַבְדְּךָ֣ כִמְהָ֗ם יַֽעֲבֹר֙ עִם־אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַעֲשֵׂה־ל֕וֹ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ט֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Let return, please, your servant, and I will die in my city, near [the] grave of my father and my mother; and look, your servant Chimham, let him cross with my lord the king, and do for him what [is] good in your eyes.

en.L: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city, near the grave of my father and my mother. But look, your servant Chimham: let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what [is] good in your eyes."
en.B: Please let your servant go back, so that I may die in my own town near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross the river with my lord the king, and treat him in whatever way seems good to you."
en.R: Please let me go back home. I want to die in my own town and be buried near my father and mother. But here is Chimham, who will serve you. Let him go across with you, Your Majesty. Do for him whatever you think is best."

es.L: Te ruego que dejes volver a tu siervo, para que muera en mi ciudad, junto al sepulcro de mi padre y de mi madre. Pero he aquí tu siervo Quimam: que pase él con mi señor el rey, y haz por él lo que [sea] bueno a tus ojos».
es.B: Te ruego que dejes volver a tu siervo, para que muera en mi propio pueblo, junto al sepulcro de mi padre y de mi madre. Pero aquí está tu siervo Quimam. Que cruce el río con mi señor el rey, y trátalo como te parezca bien».
es.R: Por favor, déjame volver a casa. Quiero morir en mi propio pueblo y que me entierren junto a mi padre y mi madre. Pero aquí está Quimam, que te servirá. Deja que él cruce contigo, mi rey. Haz por él lo que creas mejor».

fr.L: Que ton serviteur s’en retourne, je te prie, et je mourrai dans ma ville, près du tombeau de mon père et de ma mère. Mais voici ton serviteur Kimham : qu’il passe avec mon seigneur le roi, et fais pour lui ce qui [est] bon à tes yeux. »
fr.B: Je t’en prie, laisse ton serviteur s’en retourner, pour que je meure dans ma ville, près du tombeau de mon père et de ma mère. Mais voici ton serviteur Kimham. Qu’il passe le fleuve avec mon seigneur le roi ; traite-le comme bon te semblera. »
fr.R: S’il te plaît, laisse-moi rentrer chez moi. Je veux mourir dans ma ville et être enterré près de mon père et de ma mère. Mais voici Kimham, qui te servira. Laisse-le partir avec toi, mon roi. Fais pour lui ce que tu penses être le mieux. »

vi.L: Xin cho đầy tớ của vua trở về, để tôi chết trong thành mình, gần mộ cha mẹ tôi. Nhưng kìa, đầy tớ của vua là Kim-ham, xin cho nó qua sông với chúa tôi là vua, và xin vua làm cho nó điều gì tốt trong mắt vua."
vi.B: Xin cho đầy tớ của vua trở về, để tôi được chết tại quê mình, gần mộ cha mẹ tôi. Nhưng đây là Kim-ham, đầy tớ của vua. Xin cho nó qua sông với bệ hạ, và xin bệ hạ đối đãi với nó tùy ý bệ hạ."
vi.R: Xin đức vua cho tôi về nhà. Tôi muốn chết tại quê mình và được chôn gần mộ cha mẹ tôi. Nhưng đây là Kim-ham, nó sẽ phục vụ đức vua. Xin cho nó đi qua sông với đức vua. Xin đức vua làm cho nó điều gì đức vua thấy là tốt nhất."

decisions.choice: near the grave of my father and my mother: to be buried with his family
decisions.reason: To be buried in the family tomb was a great wish in Israel (Genesis 49:29-31; 50:25). Barzillai wants to die at home and lie with his parents.

decisions.choice: Chimham: probably Barzillai's son
decisions.reason: The text does not say who Chimham was, but David later asks Solomon to show kindness to "the sons of Barzillai" (1 Kings 2:7), and a place near Bethlehem is later called after Chimham (Jeremiah 41:17), perhaps land the king gave him.

decisions.choice: your servant Chimham: offered for the king's service
decisions.reason: Barzillai offers Chimham in his place, to go to court and receive the king's favor.

decisions.choice: and be buried
decisions.reason: Readable adds "be buried" to explain why the grave of his parents matters. It says "me" for "your servant".

decisions.choice: Kimham
decisions.reason: The French transcription with "k" for the Hebrew kaf, as in Akish and Makir; kept for both books.

decisions.choice: Quimam
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish spelling of the name, used again in verses 39 and 41.

decisions.choice: "Kim-ham"
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese form; kept in verse 41, where the Hebrew spells the name differently (meaning decision there).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אִתִּי֙ יַעֲבֹ֣ר כִּמְהָ֔ם וַאֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂה־לּ֔וֹ אֶת־הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־תִּבְחַ֥ר עָלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king, with me will cross Chimham, and I, I will do for him the good in your eyes; and all that you choose of me I will do for you.

en.L: And the king said, "With me Chimham shall cross over, and I will do for him what [is] good in your eyes; and all that you choose [to ask] of me I will do for you."
en.B: The king answered, "Chimham will cross with me, and I myself will do for him whatever you think good. And anything you ask of me, I will do for you."
en.R: The king answered, "Chimham will come with me, and I will do for him whatever you think is best. And I will do anything you ask me to do for you."

es.L: Y el rey dijo: «Conmigo pasará Quimam, y yo haré por él lo que [sea] bueno a tus ojos; y todo lo que escojas [pedirme] lo haré por ti».
es.B: El rey respondió: «Quimam cruzará conmigo, y yo mismo haré por él lo que a ti te parezca bien. Y todo lo que me pidas, lo haré por ti».
es.R: El rey respondió: «Quimam vendrá conmigo, y haré por él lo que tú creas mejor. Y haré por ti todo lo que me pidas».

fr.L: Et le roi dit : « Avec moi passera Kimham, et moi, je ferai pour lui ce qui [est] bon à tes yeux ; et tout ce que tu choisiras [de me demander], je le ferai pour toi. »
fr.B: Le roi répondit : « Kimham passera avec moi, et je ferai moi-même pour lui ce que tu jugeras bon. Et tout ce que tu me demanderas, je le ferai pour toi. »
fr.R: Le roi a répondu : « Kimham viendra avec moi, et je ferai pour lui ce que tu penses être le mieux. Et je ferai pour toi tout ce que tu me demanderas. »

vi.L: Vua nói: "Kim-ham sẽ qua sông với ta, và chính ta sẽ làm cho nó điều gì tốt trong mắt ông; và mọi điều ông chọn [xin] nơi ta, ta sẽ làm cho ông."
vi.B: Vua đáp: "Kim-ham sẽ qua sông với ta, và chính ta sẽ làm cho nó mọi điều ông thấy là tốt. Còn ông xin ta điều gì, ta cũng sẽ làm cho ông."
vi.R: Vua đáp: "Kim-ham sẽ đi với ta, và ta sẽ làm cho nó mọi điều ông thấy là tốt nhất. Ông xin ta làm gì cho ông, ta cũng sẽ làm."

decisions.choice: with me ... and I: the king's own pledge
decisions.reason: "With me" stands first, and "I" is added before the verb. The king takes Barzillai's request on himself: he will see to Chimham personally.

decisions.choice: all that you choose of me: anything you want to ask of me
decisions.reason: The phrase means to lay a request on someone. Barzillai may name any favor and the king will grant it.

decisions.choice: [to ask] (Literal); ask (Balanced)
decisions.reason: English needs a verb of asking for the request that "choose of me" implies.

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר כָּל־הָעָ֛ם אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עָבָ֑ר וַיִּשַּׁ֨ק הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ לְבַרְזִלַּי֙ וַיְבָ֣רֲכֵ֔הוּ וַיָּ֖שָׁב לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And crossed all the people the Jordan, and the king crossed; and kissed the king Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his place.

en.L: And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his place.
en.B: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed too. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai went back to his home.
en.R: Then all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed too. The king kissed Barzillai goodbye and asked God to bless him. Then Barzillai went back home.

es.L: Y todo el pueblo pasó el Jordán, y el rey pasó. Y el rey besó a Barzilai y lo bendijo, y él volvió a su lugar.
es.B: Así que todo el pueblo cruzó el Jordán, y el rey también cruzó. El rey besó a Barzilai y lo bendijo, y Barzilai regresó a su casa.
es.R: Entonces todo el pueblo cruzó el Jordán, y el rey también cruzó. El rey se despidió de Barzilai con un beso y le pidió a Dios que lo bendijera. Luego Barzilai regresó a su casa.

fr.L: Et tout le peuple passa le Jourdain, et le roi passa. Et le roi embrassa Barzillaï et le bénit, et il retourna chez lui.
fr.B: Tout le peuple passa donc le Jourdain, et le roi passa aussi. Le roi embrassa Barzillaï et le bénit, et Barzillaï retourna chez lui.
fr.R: Ensuite, tout le peuple a traversé le Jourdain, et le roi a traversé aussi. Le roi a embrassé Barzillaï pour lui dire au revoir, et il a demandé à Dieu de le bénir. Puis Barzillaï est rentré chez lui.

vi.L: Toàn dân qua sông Giô-đanh, và vua cũng qua. Vua hôn Bát-xi-lai và chúc phước cho ông, rồi ông trở về chỗ mình.
vi.B: Vậy toàn dân qua sông Giô-đanh, và vua cũng qua. Vua hôn Bát-xi-lai và chúc phước cho ông, rồi Bát-xi-lai trở về nhà.
vi.R: Rồi toàn dân qua sông Giô-đanh, và vua cũng qua sông. Vua hôn từ biệt Bát-xi-lai và cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho ông. Rồi Bát-xi-lai trở về nhà.

decisions.choice: kissed and blessed: a farewell
decisions.reason: A kiss and a blessing were the way to say goodbye to someone dear (Genesis 31:55). To bless someone was to ask God's good on them.

decisions.choice: he returned to his place: Barzillai went home
decisions.reason: The subject is Barzillai, who goes back to Rogelim as he asked (verse 38).

decisions.choice: all the people: those who had gone with the king
decisions.reason: Here "the people" are the whole company with David, his army together with his household and officials.

decisions.choice: Barzillai
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Barzillai, since "he" could be taken as the king.

decisions.choice: goodbye; asked God to bless him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the kiss and the blessing meant, following meaning decision m1.

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֔לָה וְכִמְהָ֖ן עָבַ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ וְכָל־עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙ הֶעֱבִ֣ירוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְגַ֕ם חֲצִ֖י עַ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went on the king to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him; and all [the] people of Judah brought over the king, and also half [the] people of Israel.

en.L: And the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him. And all the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.
en.B: The king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went with him. All the people of Judah had brought the king across, and half the people of Israel as well.
en.R: The king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went with him. All the people of Judah had come to bring the king across the river, and half the people of Israel came too.

es.L: Y el rey siguió hasta Gilgal, y Quimam siguió con él. Y todo el pueblo de Judá hizo pasar al rey, y también la mitad del pueblo de Israel.
es.B: El rey siguió hasta Gilgal, y Quimam fue con él. Todo el pueblo de Judá había acompañado al rey en el cruce, y también la mitad del pueblo de Israel.
es.R: El rey siguió hasta Gilgal, y Quimam fue con él. Toda la gente de Judá había venido para ayudar al rey a cruzar el río, y también vino la mitad de la gente de Israel.

fr.L: Et le roi passa à Guilgal, et Kimham passa avec lui. Et tout le peuple de Juda avait fait passer le roi, et aussi la moitié du peuple d’Israël.
fr.B: Le roi continua jusqu’à Guilgal, et Kimham l’accompagnait. Tout le peuple de Juda avait fait passer le fleuve au roi, et la moitié du peuple d’Israël aussi.
fr.R: Le roi a continué jusqu’à Guilgal, et Kimham est allé avec lui. Tout le peuple de Juda était venu aider le roi à traverser le fleuve, et la moitié du peuple d’Israël était venue aussi.

vi.L: Vua đi tiếp đến Ghinh-ganh, và Kim-ham đi tiếp với vua. Toàn dân Giu-đa đưa vua sang, cùng với một nửa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Vua đi tiếp đến Ghinh-ganh, và Kim-ham đi theo vua. Toàn dân Giu-đa đã đưa vua qua sông, cùng với một nửa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Vua đi tiếp đến Ghinh-ganh, và Kim-ham đi với vua. Toàn dân Giu-đa đã đến đưa vua qua sông, và một nửa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng đến.

decisions.choice: went on: passed on from the river
decisions.reason: The verb used throughout for crossing the Jordan here means passing on from the river to Gilgal.

decisions.choice: Chimham: the same man as in verses 38-39
decisions.reason: The Hebrew spells his name with a final n here instead of m. It is the same person.

decisions.choice: Judah and half of Israel: the tribes divided
decisions.reason: "Israel" here means the tribes other than Judah. Only some of them had come in time to escort the king, which leads to the quarrel that follows.

decisions.choice: had brought
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "had" to show that the escort had already met the king at the river (verse 16).

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֛ה כָּל־אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּאִ֣ים אֶל־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ מַדּוּעַ֩ גְּנָב֨וּךָ אַחֵ֜ינוּ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּעֲבִ֨רוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְאֶת־בֵּיתוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י דָוִ֖ד עִמּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And look, all [the] men of Israel [were] coming to the king, and they said to the king, why have stolen you our brothers, [the] men of Judah, and brought over the king and his household [over] the Jordan, and all [the] men of David with him?

en.L: And look, all the men of Israel were coming to the king, and they said to the king, "Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king and his household across the Jordan, and all the men of David with him?"
en.B: Just then the men of Israel all came to the king and said to him, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away? Why did they take the king and his household over the Jordan, along with all David's men?"
en.R: Then all the men of Israel came to the king. They said to him, "Why did our relatives, the men of Judah, take you away from us? Why did they bring you and your family across the Jordan, with all your men, and leave us out?"

es.L: Y he aquí, todos los hombres de Israel venían al rey, y dijeron al rey: «¿Por qué te han robado nuestros hermanos, los hombres de Judá, y han hecho pasar el Jordán al rey y a su casa, y a todos los hombres de David con él?».
es.B: En eso llegaron todos los hombres de Israel adonde estaba el rey y le dijeron: «¿Por qué nuestros hermanos, los hombres de Judá, te han llevado a escondidas? ¿Por qué hicieron cruzar el Jordán al rey y a su familia, junto con todos los hombres de David?».
es.R: Entonces todos los hombres de Israel vinieron a ver al rey. Le dijeron: «¿Por qué nuestros parientes, los hombres de Judá, te apartaron de nosotros? ¿Por qué te hicieron cruzar el Jordán a ti y a tu familia, con todos tus hombres, y nos dejaron fuera a nosotros?».

fr.L: Et voici, tous les hommes d’Israël vinrent vers le roi, et ils dirent au roi : « Pourquoi nos frères, les hommes de Juda, t’ont-ils enlevé et ont-ils fait passer le Jourdain au roi et à sa maison, et à tous les hommes de David avec lui ? »
fr.B: À ce moment, tous les hommes d’Israël vinrent trouver le roi et lui dirent : « Pourquoi nos frères, les hommes de Juda, t’ont-ils enlevé ? Pourquoi ont-ils fait passer le Jourdain au roi et à sa maison, ainsi qu’à tous les hommes de David ? »
fr.R: Alors tous les hommes d’Israël sont venus voir le roi. Ils lui ont dit : « Pourquoi nos frères, les hommes de Juda, t’ont-ils pris pour eux seuls ? Pourquoi ont-ils fait traverser le Jourdain à toi et à ta famille, avec tous tes hommes, sans nous ? »

vi.L: Kìa, mọi người Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp vua và nói với vua: "Sao anh em chúng tôi, là người Giu-đa, đã đánh cắp vua đi, và đưa vua cùng gia đình vua qua sông Giô-đanh, cùng tất cả người của Đa-vít với vua?"
vi.B: Ngay lúc ấy mọi người Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp vua và thưa: "Sao anh em chúng tôi là người Giu-đa lại cướp lấy bệ hạ? Sao họ lại đưa bệ hạ cùng hoàng gia qua sông Giô-đanh, cùng với tất cả người của Đa-vít?"
vi.R: Rồi mọi người Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp vua. Họ thưa: "Sao bà con chúng tôi là người Giu-đa lại giành đức vua khỏi chúng tôi? Sao họ lại đưa đức vua và gia đình đức vua qua sông Giô-đanh cùng với tất cả người của đức vua, mà bỏ chúng tôi ra ngoài?"

decisions.choice: stolen you away: taken you for themselves, without us
decisions.reason: The verb means to steal. The men of Israel complain that Judah has taken the king behind their backs. The same root described the army slipping into Mahanaim in verse 4.

decisions.choice: our brothers: fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: "Brothers" means kin in the wide sense: all the tribes were one people, descended from Jacob.

decisions.choice: the king ... you: speaking to the king about the king
decisions.reason: The men of Israel speak to David as "you" and also, politely, as "the king" in the third person.

decisions.choice: take you away from us; and leave us out
decisions.reason: Readable states the complaint implied by "stolen", that the north had no part in it. It uses "you" for "the king" and "your men" for "the men of David".

source.text: וַיַּעַן֩ כָּל־אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה עַל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּֽי־קָר֤וֹב הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֵלַ֔י וְלָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ חָרָ֣ה לְךָ֔ עַל־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה הֶאָכ֤וֹל אָכַ֨לְנוּ֙ מִן־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־נִשֵּׂ֥את נִשָּׂ֖א לָֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And answered all [the] men of Judah to [the] men of Israel, because near [is] the king to me; and why this is it hot to you over this matter? Eating have we eaten from the king, or carrying has [anything] been carried for us?

en.L: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king [is] near to me. And why [is] it burning to you over this matter? Have we eaten at all from the king, or has [anything] been carried off for us at all?"
en.B: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "We did it because the king is our close relative. Why are you so angry about this? Have we eaten anything at the king's expense? Have we been given any gift?"
en.R: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "We did it because the king is from our own tribe. Why are you angry about this? The king has not paid for our food. He has not given us any gifts."

es.L: Y todos los hombres de Judá respondieron a los hombres de Israel: «Porque el rey [es] pariente cercano mío. ¿Y por qué {{plural_you:les|os}} arde esto? ¿Acaso hemos comido algo del rey, o se nos ha llevado [algún] regalo?».
es.B: Todos los hombres de Judá les respondieron a los hombres de Israel: «Lo hicimos porque el rey es pariente cercano nuestro. ¿Por qué se {{plural_you:enojan|enojáis}} tanto por esto? ¿Hemos comido algo a costa del rey? ¿Se nos ha dado algún regalo?».
es.R: Todos los hombres de Judá les respondieron a los hombres de Israel: «Lo hicimos porque el rey es de nuestra propia tribu. ¿Por qué se {{plural_you:enojan|enojáis}} por esto? El rey no nos ha pagado la comida. No nos ha dado ningún regalo».

fr.L: Et tous les hommes de Juda répondirent aux hommes d’Israël : « C’est que le roi m’[est] proche. Et pourquoi cela te brûle-t-il au sujet de cette affaire ? Avons-nous mangé quoi que ce soit aux dépens du roi, ou nous a-t-on emporté quoi que ce soit ? »
fr.B: Tous les hommes de Juda répondirent aux hommes d’Israël : « Nous l’avons fait parce que le roi est notre proche parent. Pourquoi cette affaire vous met-elle en colère ? Avons-nous vécu aux frais du roi ? Avons-nous reçu de lui quelque cadeau ? »
fr.R: Tous les hommes de Juda ont répondu aux hommes d’Israël : « Nous l’avons fait parce que le roi est de notre tribu. Pourquoi êtes-vous en colère ? Le roi ne nous a pas payé notre nourriture. Il ne nous a fait aucun cadeau. »

vi.L: Mọi người Giu-đa đáp lại người Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Vì vua gần gũi với tôi. Sao các anh lại nổi nóng về việc này? Chúng tôi có ăn gì của vua chăng, hay có ai mang [gì] đến cho chúng tôi chăng?"
vi.B: Mọi người Giu-đa đáp lại người Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Chúng tôi làm vậy vì vua là bà con gần của chúng tôi. Sao các anh lại tức giận về chuyện này? Chúng tôi có được vua đãi ăn gì đâu? Chúng tôi có được ban quà gì đâu?"
vi.R: Mọi người Giu-đa đáp lại người Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Chúng tôi làm vậy vì vua thuộc chi tộc của chúng tôi. Sao các anh lại giận về chuyện này? Vua đâu có trả tiền ăn cho chúng tôi. Vua cũng đâu có cho chúng tôi quà gì."

decisions.choice: near to me: closely related
decisions.reason: The word for near is used of a close relative (Ruth 2:20; 3:12). David was of the tribe of Judah. The men of Judah speak as one, "me".

decisions.choice: is it hot to you: are you angry
decisions.reason: Anger in Hebrew is pictured as burning or heat.

decisions.choice: have we eaten at all, or has anything been carried off: denying any reward
alternatives: has anything been taken by us
decisions.reason: Both verbs are doubled, which strengthens the question: "Have we in any way eaten ...?" Judah denies having gained anything from the king for their loyalty. The second verb means to lift or carry; it may mean a gift or portion carried to them, as portions were carried from a king's table (Genesis 43:34).

decisions.choice: our close relative (Balanced); from our own tribe (Readable); we, us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "we" and "us" for the collective "I" and "me", and add "We did it" so the answer fits the question it replies to.

decisions.choice: statements for questions
decisions.reason: Readable states the denials that the questions imply.

decisions.choice: "me", "te" (singular) for each side
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew’s singular, each tribe speaking as one man; Balanced and Readable use the plural, as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:les|os}}; se {{plural_you:enojan|enojáis}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the men of Israel as one man ('to you', singular). Spanish addresses them as the group they are, with the plural_you setting; Literal keeps the singular 'mío' for Judah's own voice, as the English Literal keeps 'me'.

decisions.choice: the tribes say "chúng tôi" and "các anh" to each other
decisions.reason: Like the English Balanced and Readable, Vietnamese uses plural forms for the collective "I"; "các anh" fits a quarrel between kinsmen of equal standing.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַן אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֩ אֶת־אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עֶֽשֶׂר־יָד֨וֹת לִ֣י בַמֶּלֶךְ֮ וְגַם־בְּדָוִד֮ אֲנִ֣י מִמְּךָ֒ וּמַדּ֨וּעַ֙ הֱקִלֹּתַ֔נִי וְלֹא־הָיָ֨ה דְבָרִ֥י רִאשׁ֛וֹן לִ֖י לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶת־מַלְכִּ֑י וַיִּ֨קֶשׁ֙ דְּבַר־אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדְּבַ֖ר אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And answered [the] man of Israel [the] man of Judah, and said, ten hands to me in the king, and also in David I [am more] than you; and why have you treated me lightly? And was not my word first, for me, to bring back my king? And was hard [the] word of [the] man of Judah more than [the] word of [the] man of Israel.

en.L: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, "Ten hands in the king [belong] to me, and also in David I [have more] than you. And why have you treated me lightly? And was not my word the first, for me to bring back my king?" But the word of the men of Judah was harder than the word of the men of Israel.
en.B: The men of Israel replied to the men of Judah, "Ten shares in the king are ours, and in David too our share is larger than yours. So why do you treat us as if we did not matter? Was it not we who first said that our king should be brought back?" But the men of Judah answered more fiercely than the men of Israel.
en.R: The men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "There are ten tribes of us, so we have ten times as much right to the king as you do. David belongs to us more than to you. Why do you treat us as if we were not important? We were the first ones to talk about bringing our king back!" But the men of Judah argued even more harshly than the men of Israel.

es.L: Y los hombres de Israel respondieron a los hombres de Judá y dijeron: «Diez partes en el rey [son] mías, y también en David [tengo más] que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¿Por qué, pues, me {{plural_you:han|habéis}} tenido en poco? ¿Y no fue mi palabra la primera, para hacer volver a mi rey?». Pero la palabra de los hombres de Judá fue más dura que la palabra de los hombres de Israel.
es.B: Los hombres de Israel les respondieron a los hombres de Judá: «Diez partes del rey son nuestras, y también en David tenemos más parte que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¿Por qué, entonces, nos {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}} como si no contáramos? ¿No fuimos nosotros los primeros en decir que había que hacer volver a nuestro rey?». Pero los hombres de Judá respondieron con más dureza que los hombres de Israel.
es.R: Los hombres de Israel les respondieron a los hombres de Judá: «Nosotros somos diez tribus, así que tenemos diez veces más derecho al rey que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. David es más nuestro que {{plural_you:suyo|vuestro}}. ¿Por qué nos {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}} como si no fuéramos importantes? ¡Nosotros fuimos los primeros en hablar de traer de vuelta a nuestro rey!». Pero los hombres de Judá discutieron con más dureza todavía que los hombres de Israel.

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Israël répondirent aux hommes de Juda et dirent : « J’ai dix mains dans le roi, et même en David [j’ai plus] que toi. Et pourquoi m’as-tu méprisé ? Ma parole n’a-t-elle pas été la première, pour moi, à ramener mon roi ? » Mais la parole des hommes de Juda fut plus dure que la parole des hommes d’Israël.
fr.B: Les hommes d’Israël répliquèrent aux hommes de Juda : « Nous avons dix parts sur le roi, et même sur David nous avons plus de droits que vous. Pourquoi nous traitez-vous comme si nous ne comptions pas ? N’est-ce pas nous qui avons parlé les premiers de ramener notre roi ? » Mais les hommes de Juda répondirent plus durement encore que les hommes d’Israël.
fr.R: Les hommes d’Israël ont répondu aux hommes de Juda : « Nous sommes dix tribus, donc nous avons dix fois plus de droits sur le roi que vous. David est à nous plus qu’à vous. Pourquoi nous traitez-vous comme si nous n’étions pas importants ? C’est nous qui avons parlé les premiers de ramener notre roi ! » Mais les hommes de Juda ont parlé encore plus durement que les hommes d’Israël.

vi.L: Người Y-sơ-ra-ên đáp lại người Giu-đa và nói: "Tôi có mười phần nơi vua, và nơi Đa-vít tôi cũng [có phần nhiều] hơn các anh. Sao các anh lại coi thường tôi? Chẳng phải lời tôi là lời đầu tiên, để đem vua tôi trở về sao?" Nhưng lời của người Giu-đa còn gay gắt hơn lời của người Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Người Y-sơ-ra-ên đáp lại người Giu-đa: "Chúng tôi có mười phần nơi vua, và nơi Đa-vít phần của chúng tôi cũng nhiều hơn các anh. Vậy sao các anh lại coi thường chúng tôi? Chẳng phải chính chúng tôi đã đề nghị trước tiên việc đưa vua mình trở về sao?" Nhưng người Giu-đa đáp lại còn gay gắt hơn người Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Người Y-sơ-ra-ên đáp lại người Giu-đa: "Chúng tôi có mười chi tộc, nên chúng tôi có quyền đối với vua gấp mười lần các anh. Đa-vít thuộc về chúng tôi nhiều hơn là thuộc về các anh. Sao các anh lại coi chúng tôi như không đáng kể? Chính chúng tôi là những người đầu tiên nói đến việc đưa vua mình trở về!" Nhưng người Giu-đa còn cãi lại gay gắt hơn người Y-sơ-ra-ên.

decisions.choice: ten hands in the king: ten shares, for the ten tribes
decisions.reason: "Hand" can mean a share or part (Genesis 43:34; 47:24). The northern tribes, counted as ten, claim ten parts of the king against Judah's one.

decisions.choice: and also in David I have more than you: following the Hebrew
alternatives: and I am firstborn rather than you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "and also in David". The ancient Greek translation reads "and I am the firstborn rather than you", which in Hebrew differs by a few letters, and refers to Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, among the northern tribes. This translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: treated me lightly: treated me with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to make light of someone, to count them of little weight. It is from the same root as the word for cursing used of Shimei (verse 22).

decisions.choice: the word of the men of Judah was harder: the quarrel that leads to revolt
decisions.reason: The harsh words lead straight into Sheba's call, "We have no share in David" (20:1), and foreshadow the split of the kingdom (1 Kings 12:16).

decisions.choice: we, us, our for I, me, my
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plural pronouns for the men of Israel, who speak as one, "I". Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: There are ten tribes of us; a statement for the last question
decisions.reason: Readable explains the "ten shares" from meaning decision m1 and states the claim the last question implies.
